Job Description

Overview

The Staff Software Engineer, Voice Connectivity Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates the connectivity layer between a customer's existing telephony and CCaaS environment and the ServiceNow Voice ecosystem. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: mapping a customer's SIP trunks, CTI integrations, and CCaaS-specific APIs, building and hardening the signaling, media, and event integrations that connect those systems to ServiceNow's Voice/CTI and Native Voice Controls platform, and proving through testing and production monitoring that calls connect, stay connected, and hand off cleanly under real network and carrier conditions. This is not an agent-building role — the engineer is not primarily authoring the prompts or instructions that drive voice AI agent behavior — but it is the foundation those agents run on: without a reliable connectivity layer, no agent, however well designed, can reach a live caller.

Two things follow. First, correctness here is measured in call setup success, audio quality, latency, and failover behavior rather than model output — the engineer's product is a connection that has to hold up under real carrier, network, and vendor conditions, not just in a reference environment. Second, because every customer's telephony and CCaaS setup differs — different SIP providers, media gateways, authentication schemes, and CCaaS vendor quirks — the engineer must design integrations that are resilient and diagnosable, with clear failure signals when a segment of the call path breaks, rather than integrations that only work against the reference stack.

  What You Get to Do

  • Build the connectivity layer. Design, build, and operate the SIP trunking, signaling, and media integrations that connect a customer's telephony and CCaaS platform to ServiceNow's Voice/CTI and Native Voice Controls ecosystem.
  • Integrate with CCaaS and telephony platforms. Implement and harden integrations using the common patterns of SIP trunking and signaling, WebSocket and streaming media APIs, and real-time audio and event interfaces — across CCaaS providers such as Genesys, NICE, Five9, Amazon Connect, and Twilio, as well as traditional CTI/PBX and carrier setups.
  • Own call path reliability. Design for call setup success, failover, and graceful degradation across carriers, media gateways, and network conditions; instrument and monitor the connectivity layer for latency, jitter, packet loss, and dropped-call causes.
  • Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the customer's environment. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — mapping their existing architecture, standing up and tuning the connection into ServiceNow's Voice ecosystem, and troubleshooting live issues on their network and vendor stack.
  • Feed the Voice AI agent layer cleanly. Ensure the audio, signaling, and event streams the connectivity layer delivers are clean, well-formed, and low-latency enough for the voice AI agents running on ServiceNow's Voice ecosystem to operate correctly — partnering with agent engineering rather than building the agents yourself.
  • Design for security and compliance on the call path. Implement SIP security, media encryption, authentication, and least-privilege access across the connectivity layer, and account for what regulated or high-security customer environments require.
  • Specify precisely and direct engineering work. Convert customer telephony and CCaaS requirements into testable specifications and integration runbooks with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into implementable tasks and review the result for correctness and maintainability.
  • Own quality and reliability in production. Monitor connectivity health across live customer deployments, triage call-path incidents, and feed recurring failure patterns back into architecture and runbooks.
  • Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, voice AI agent engineers, and platform teams — Voice/CTI, CCaaS, and Native Voice Controls — to define integration requirements, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly.

Qualifications

To Be Successful in This Role

Experience

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production telephony or CCaaS integrations at a Staff Software Engineer level, including hands-on delivery of connectivity between third-party telephony/CCaaS platforms and a hosted or cloud service. Direct, hands-on experience integrating with CCaaS platforms using common patterns — SIP trunking and signaling, WebSocket and streaming media APIs, and real-time audio interfaces — across multiple CCaaS providers, is required. Demonstrated technical leadership is expected at this level: setting architectural direction across teams, mentoring engineers, and driving cross-team integration decisions on voice and telephony systems. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their telephony and contact center environment, is required; prior forward deployed experience is an advantage. Typically 8+ years of production software experience, with several years focused on telephony, CTI, or real-time communications systems.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice and telephony connectivity.

Key Competencies, Skills, and Experience

  • Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing.
  • CCaaS and telephony integration patterns. Hands-on experience integrating with CCaaS platforms and telephony infrastructure using SIP trunking and signaling, WebSocket and streaming media APIs, and real-time audio interfaces, across multiple providers such as Genesys, NICE, Five9, Amazon Connect, and Twilio, as well as traditional CTI/PBX systems.
  • Real-time communications and media handling. Practical knowledge of SIP, RTP/SRTP, WebRTC, codecs, media gateways, and the latency, jitter, and packet-loss characteristics of live audio.
  • Call path reliability and observability. Ability to design for failover and graceful degradation across carriers and vendors, and to instrument, monitor, and diagnose connectivity issues in production.
  • Voice platform architecture. Working knowledge of how a hosted voice and agent ecosystem — such as ServiceNow's Voice/CTI and Native Voice Controls — consumes audio, signaling, and event streams, enough to design an integration the platform can reliably use without building the agent logic itself.
  • Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define integration and connectivity problems rigorously enough for another engineer to implement correctly, and sound judgment on build-versus-integrate tradeoffs across vendor ecosystems.
  • Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to telephony integrations — SIP security, media encryption, call-recording and PII handling, over-broad access — translated into concrete guardrails and monitoring.
  • Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers.

Desired Experience

  • Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.
  • Carrier and infrastructure depth. Experience with SIP trunk provisioning, PSTN/carrier relationships, number porting, and codec-level audio handling below the application layer.
  • CCaaS platform specialization. Deep, hands-on experience with one or more major CCaaS platforms — such as Genesys, NICE, Five9, or Amazon Connect — beyond generic integration patterns.
  • Observability tooling. Experience with tracing, monitoring, and analysis tooling for real-time communications systems, and analysis of production call and connectivity data at scale.
  • Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, or enterprise IT/telephony operations, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.
  • Years of Experience. At least 8 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Forward Deployed Engineer, Voice AI Agent Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates voice AI agents whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret caller intent over a live audio channel, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the caller's behalf. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: shaping ambiguous call flows and telephony requirements into precise specifications, authoring the instructions and prompts that govern voice agent behavior, proving through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly on real calls. This is not a machine learning or AI research role — the engineer does not train foundation or speech models — but it is distinct from traditional software engineering, where systems follow deterministic call-flow logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime. 

Two things follow, and voice makes both harder. First, the agent's most important logic often lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, and guardrails — which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code, while also holding up under what a spoken channel adds: turn-taking, barge-in, and disambiguating what speech recognition got wrong. Second, because behavior is probabilistic and happens live on a call, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale — including latency, containment, and transcription accuracy — rather than by asserting fixed outputs, making automated evaluation a first-class engineering activity rather than a quality-assurance afterthought. The engineer owns the correctness of what ships to a live caller, whether a human or an agent produced it. 

What You Get to Do in this role: 

  • Build voice AI agents. Design and ship agentic voice applications — intent interpretation, multi-step reasoning, tool invocation, and action on the caller's behalf — together with the CTI, CCaaS, and telephony integrations that make them usable in production. 

  • Design AI-driven autonomous voice workflows. Decompose call flows and business processes into the steps and decision points a voice agent can execute — determining where autonomy is appropriate, where a live-agent handoff is required, and how misrecognition, retries, and escalation are handled. 

  • Engineer for what voice demands. Build experiences that hold context across turns, manage barge-in and interruption, recover gracefully from speech-recognition error, disambiguate caller intent, and confirm before consequential actions — all within the latency budget a live call imposes. 

  • Author and maintain voice agent instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern voice agent behavior — as engineering artifacts under review and regression coverage, not configuration text. 

  • Engineer prompts for reliability rather than demo quality. Iterate prompts against measured call outcomes: task decomposition, golden call transcripts, structured output schemas, grounding and citation, graceful hand-back to a human agent, and the token and latency cost that directly shapes caller experience. 

  • Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic voice behavior. Design and operate the evaluation that makes change safe on a live channel — golden call datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring calibrated to human QA review, CI gates, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, grounding, and tool-selection testing specific to voice. 

  • Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents. Convert customer call-flow and telephony requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and review agent output for correctness and maintainability. You own the result regardless of what produced it. 

  • Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the voice stack. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — building against their call data, integrations, and channels, tuning instructions and evaluation sets against live traffic, and returning with evidence that improves the product. 

  • Own quality, safety, and reliability on live calls. Monitor call containment, hallucination, unsafe actions, and transcription accuracy; defend against prompt injection and data leakage on live calls; and feed production call failures back into specifications and evaluation sets. 

  • Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, designers and platform teams to define success criteria, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly. 

Qualifications

To Be Successful in This Role:

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production voice applications, including hands-on delivery of AI-native voice agent features that real callers depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts for voice, designing AI-driven autonomous call workflows, and building the evaluation and testing that verifies them against live call traffic, is required. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their voice and contact center environment, is required. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.  

Education:Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice AI agents. 

Key Competencies, Skills, and Experience 

  • Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing. 

  • AI native voice application development. Hands-on experience building applications where model-driven behavior is central — agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling the latency, cost, and failure modes unique to a live audio channel. 

  • AI-driven autonomous workflow design. Demonstrated experience designing workflows in which voice agents carry out multi-step call processes with limited supervision: call-flow decomposition, decision points and autonomy boundaries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, exception and retry handling, and observability over what the agent did and why. 

  • Voice and telephony platform expertise. Practical experience with telephony integration, speech recognition and synthesis, and streaming audio — including the barge-in, turn-taking, and confirmation patterns a live call requires. 

  • Agentic instruction authoring. Demonstrated skill writing and maintaining the natural-language logic that governs voice agent behavior — instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and refusal and escalation rules — with versioning, review, and regression coverage applied as they would be to code. 

  • Prompt engineering. Intent-driven prompt design tuned for voice: decomposition, golden and few-shot examples, structured output and schema enforcement, grounding and citation, and disciplined iteration against call-level evaluation results rather than impressions. 

  • Evaluation and testing of non-deterministic voice systems. Ability to build measurable frameworks assessing call quality, agent behavior, tool-selection accuracy, and regression risk — golden call datasets, scenario suites, model-as-judge scoring with human QA calibration, continuous evaluation pipelines, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, and grounding testing. 

  • Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define call-flow problems rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements them correctly, and to decide soundly when to solve a problem in code, in instructions, or by delegating to an agent. 

  • Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to AI-integrated voice applications — prompt injection, sensitive-data and call-recording leakage, over-broad tool access, unsafe autonomous action — translated into concrete guardrails, least-privilege controls, and monitoring. 

  • Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, judgment about when a fast local solution is right and when to hold out for the durable one, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers. 

Desired Experience 

  • Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment. 

  • Voice and contact center technology. Telephony and contact center platforms, IVR, speech recognition and synthesis, streaming audio, and real-time latency optimization. 

  • Conversation design partnership. Experience working alongside conversation or content designers, contributing to dialogue flow, tone, and error-recovery design. 

  • Evaluation and observability tooling. Evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production call transcripts at scale. 

  • Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, sales, or enterprise workflow, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it. 

  • Years of Experience. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Team 

The Architecture Consulting & Engineering Services (ACES) team is a security-focused consulting and engineering organization that partners with many of ServiceNow's largest and most highly regulated customers. We help security teams understand, evaluate, and securely adopt the ServiceNow platform, AI capabilities, and emerging technologies. 

Our mission is to establish ServiceNow as a trusted security partner by delivering deep technical guidance, security architecture expertise, threat modeling, reference architectures, and customer-facing security engineering engagement. We operate at the intersection of Security, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to accelerate platform adoption while ensuring customers can meet their security, compliance, and risk-management objectives. 

The Role 

We are seeking an experienced Applied Security Engineer to join the ACES team. 

This is not a traditional consulting role, nor is it a traditional product security role. We are looking for a hands-on security practitioner who can dive deep into cloud-native architectures, analyze distributed systems, validate security controls, conduct threat modeling exercises, and communicate effectively with customer security teams, architects, engineers, CISOs, and executives. 

You will work directly with Fortune 500 organizations, including some of the world's largest financial services and healthcare institutions, helping them securely adopt ServiceNow platform capabilities, AI solutions, cloud services, and emerging technologies. 

Success in this role requires technical depth, customer credibility, and the ability to translate complex security concepts into practical architectural guidance. 

What You Get To Do In This Role 

  • Partner directly with customer security, architecture, engineering, risk, compliance, and executive stakeholders to address security concerns and accelerate platform adoption. 
  • Develop customer-facing security reference architectures that clearly articulate trust boundaries, data flows, identity models, encryption controls, and shared responsibility models. 
  • Perform threat modeling exercises for ServiceNow products, AI services, integrations, and customer deployment architectures. 
  • Analyze security architectures across cloud-native and distributed systems environments. 
  • Lead security deep dives covering networking, identity, encryption, data protection, application security, and AI security controls. 
  • Evaluate customer security requirements and map them to ServiceNow platform capabilities and industry best practices. 
  • Work closely with Product Management, Engineering, Product Security, and Architecture teams to identify capability gaps and advocate for customer-driven improvements. 
  • Build scalable artifacts including architecture patterns, deployment guides, implementation accelerators, technical whitepapers, detection content, and security design documentation. 
  • Assess integrations involving AI, cloud services, APIs, Kubernetes environments, data platforms, and third-party technologies. 
  • Help define secure deployment patterns for emerging AI capabilities including agents, model integrations, governance controls, and data protection mechanisms. 

  • Represent ServiceNow security architecture and best practices during customer workshops, architecture reviews, executive briefings, and security assessments. 

Qualifications

To Be Successful In This Role You Have 

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in security engineering, security architecture, cloud security, application security, product security, or related disciplines. 
  • Strong understanding of core security principles including identity and access management; authentication and authorization; network security; cryptography and key management; data protection and privacy; security monitoring and incident response; and secure software development. 
  • Experience assessing and securing cloud-native architectures. 
  • Strong knowledge of Kubernetes, container security, service-to-service communications, workload isolation, and modern application deployment patterns. 
  • Experience with one or more major cloud providers: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP). 
  • Experience conducting threat modeling using frameworks such as STRIDE, ATT&CK, PASTA, or similar methodologies. 
  • Ability to build and communicate architecture diagrams that clearly articulate data flows, trust boundaries, security controls, and deployment models. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage audiences ranging from engineers to CISOs. 
  • Experience presenting security recommendations and architectural guidance to customers and executive stakeholders. 
  • A curious mindset and willingness to continuously learn emerging technologies including AI, cloud-native platforms, and modern security architectures. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience supporting Fortune 500 or highly regulated enterprise customers. 
  • Experience working with financial services, healthcare, or public sector organizations. 
  • Knowledge of AI security, AI governance, model risk management, prompt injection risks, agentic systems, and emerging AI threats. 
  • Experience using AI technologies to improve security operations, threat detection, security analysis, or engineering productivity. 
  • Familiarity with JavaScript, scripting, or automation development. 
  • Experience with the ServiceNow platform. 
  • Experience developing security reference architectures, implementation patterns, or technical guidance consumed at scale. 
  • Industry certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, Azure Security Engineer, GSEC, GIAC, OSCP, or equivalent. 

Why This Role Is Unique 

This role sits at the intersection of customer engagement, security engineering, cloud architecture, and AI security. You'll help some of the world's largest organizations make security decisions that directly influence platform adoption, AI strategy, and enterprise risk management. 

You'll have the opportunity to shape product direction, influence engineering roadmaps, develop industry-leading security architectures, and help define how ServiceNow brings secure AI and cloud-native innovation to the world's most demanding customers.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer - VoIP Infrastructure you will: 

  • Contribute to the design, development and implementation of VoIP infrastructure, telephony platforms, and observability features that power AI-driven voice workloads  
  • Collaborate with engineering, Product, and infrastructure teams to ensure our voice and AI platforms perform efficiently, scale reliably, and integrate seamlessly across SIP/RTP, Kamailio, RTPEngine, and related telecom systems.  
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of the SRE practice by turning operational telephony and AI workload use cases into requirements for software tooling.  
  • Contribute to the execution of deployment and support activities for VoIP systems and AI/ML developers operating in production voice environments.  
  • Build high-quality, clean, scalable and reusable code by enforcing best practices around software engineering architecture and processes (Code Reviews, Unit testing, etc.).  
  • Work with product owners to understand detailed requirements and own your code from design, implementation, test automation, and delivery — spanning both telephony infrastructure and LLM integration layers.  
  • Experience integrating LLMs into voice platforms and real-time communication systems.  
  • Be a mentor for colleagues and help promote knowledge-sharing across telecom and AI engineering disciplines.  

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have: 

  • Hands-on experience building VoIP systems using SIP/RTP protocols;    
  • Practical knowledge of Kamailio, RTPEngine, FreeSWITCH, SBCs, and PSTN systems (or similar);  
  • Working knowledge of PSTN infrastructure and telecom protocols;  
  • Experience integrating applications on top of LLMs (using existing models, not building them);  
  • Experience in prompt engineering and developing LLM based features   
  • 4+ years of development experience with Python, GoLang, Java or similar languages.  
  • 4+ years of experience operating highly available distributed workloads on Kubernetes following a DevOps approach.   
  • Working experience building distributed systems with cloud-native software;   
  • Experience with software-defined networking, infrastructure as code and configuration management;  
  • Experience with DevOps tooling  (e.g. Helm / Ansible / Kubernetes / Prometheus /Splunk/ GitLab CI) is considered an asset  
  • Experience building software for compliance and security in regulated environments is considered an asset  
  • 4+ years of experience with infrastructure and platform operations, deployments, SRE, and DevOps with a continued focus on improving Platform health is considered an asset  

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $176,100 - $308,200, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.

title: Principal Customer Success Executive
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started in sunny San Diego, California in 2004 when a visionary engineer, Fred Luddy, saw the potential to transform how we work. Fast forward to today — ServiceNow stands as a global market leader, bringing innovative AI-enhanced technology to over 8,100 customers, including 85% of the Fortune 500®. Our intelligent cloud-based platform seamlessly connects people, systems, and processes to empower organizations to find smarter, faster, and better ways to work. But this is just the beginning of our journey. Join us as we pursue our purpose to make the world work better for everyone.

Job Description

As a trusted C-Suite / executive level advisor on ServiceNow offerings, the Principal Customer Success Executive (PCSE) owns the post-sale customer relationship, aiming to increase customer satisfaction and drive retention through Impact delivery. Principal CSEs are experienced individuals who bring a consultative, problem-solving approach to partnering with senior customer stakeholders to derive value from our platforms. They demonstrate a strong understanding of customer’s industry and specific business strategies, driving alignment between these factors and what ServiceNow can offer to enable better business outcomes for their customers. This role drives business transformation by maximizing the long-term strategic value of ServiceNow and ensuring that every aspect of the customer’s platform and capability are ready for expansion. 

They provide strategic direction and mentorship to both customers and ServiceNow teams managing complex, multi-workstream programs. They play a pivotal role in resolving escalations and mitigating risks, ensuring adoption and usage is maintained at healthy levels. Principal CSEs focus on ensuring the customer recognizes the value of the ServiceNow Platform at all levels and stages, facilitating a smooth path to both renewal and up- and cross-sell. 

Overall, Principal CSEs are responsible for fostering the relationship with C-suite level stakeholders in a smaller number of strategically important Impact accounts, with the aim of increasing customer satisfaction and driving retention and upgrades, where applicable. 

Job Responsibilities 

Lead high-complexity transformations in our largest and most strategic customers, ensuring all ServiceNow Customer Excellence roles align and deliver in accordance with governance frameworks, customer objectives, and organizational priorities; ultimately chaperoning Impact value management and demonstrating strategic oversight. 

Proactively identify professional services pipeline opportunities through product capabilities road mapping, value blueprints and adoption analysis, providing pre-sales support for funnel opportunities as requested. 

Partner with Impact team members (e.g., Customer Success Managers) leveraging the joint visibility of customer insights to create executive-ready narratives. 

Work with senior executives to shape and influence customer organizational strategy by identifying emerging trends, refining best practices, and aligning delivery approaches with evolving market demands, and providing industry-specific thought leadership. 

Drive operational consistency and excellence by standardizing delivery methodologies and ensuring adherence to governance and quality standards, interfacing with Delivery as required. 

Establish relationships with ServiceNow leaders, advocating for product evolution based on customer insights, and mentoring other Customer Success resources on transformation best practices. 

Identify areas of risk and take steps to prevent customer or revenue churn. 

Work closely with Sales Teams to define and execute product adoption and customer retention plans. 

Provide prescriptive guidance on internal project/program governance and help the customer create the appropriate governance models and ensure adherence. 

Help the customer identify incidents where contractual SLAs were missed and take necessary action. 

Improve overall customer satisfaction, as well as the satisfaction of their internal customers.

Qualifications

Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry. 

Significant experience collaborating with senior IT and business leaders, with a track record of successfully translating corporate strategy/objectives with the applied use of ServiceNow technology in the context of the client’s environment. 

PMP preferred; project management experience required. 

Minimum 15+ years in client-facing roles with a focus on account management, consulting, or transformation leadership. Experience in executive-level leadership roles, with a proven track record of influencing senior stakeholders and driving strategic outcomes, is strongly preferred. 

Experience in any of the following critical subject areas, with a demonstrated history delivering consulting services: 

IT Strategy and Planning 

IT Operations and Management 

Human Resources 

Security Operations 

Customer Service Management 

IT Processes 

IT Governance 

IT Portfolio, Program and Project Management 

IT Project Delivery (SDLC) 

Experience with project problem diagnosis, solution development, client communications, facilitation of decision making, documentation, managing client expectations, and team leadership. 

Independently leverages AI to optimize workflows, tailor customer solutions, and inform strategic decisions.  

Articulates AI system design, ethical implications, and platform use cases clearly, guiding peers and stakeholders in responsible, value-driven AI adoption.

descriptionHtml:

Job Description

The GAIL (Get AI Live) program deploys engineers directly into strategic customer engagements to drive real AI adoption and measurable value realization. The GAIL Core Team is the permanent engine behind that program: the stable foundation of institutional knowledge, tooling, and senior expertise that makes every engagement, and every rotating engineer, better than the last.

As a Principal Product Success Architect on the GAIL Core Team, you set the strategic direction for how the program scales, own the hardest engagements and escalations, and build the infrastructure and knowledge systems that raise capability across the entire practice. This role bridges technical delivery and program strategy. You lead by example on the most complex deployments while shaping how the program evolves to handle harder problems and reach more customers.

What you get to do in this role:

  • Own the most complex, escalated GAIL and Go-Live Support engagements — large-scale enterprise deployments, acquisition integrations, and high-stakes go-lives where program reputation is on the line.
  • Set the strategic direction for GAIL tooling and infrastructure — defining the next-generation capabilities the program needs and owning the roadmap to build them.
  • Own and evolve the GAIL playbook and quality standards across the entire practice — defining what great looks like and holding the line on it program-wide.
  • Drive systemic improvements across customer engagements — identifying patterns in failure modes, complexity, and escalations, and translating them into playbook changes and tooling investments.
  • Mentor and develop the Core Team engineers and high-potential rotators — actively raising the capability of the people around you and shaping the next generation of leaders.
  • Partner deeply with product, engineering leadership, and customer success to translate field signal into product and program improvements.
  • Represent the program in customer-facing strategic conversations and executive engagements.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, with substantial depth in both enterprise product work and hands-on customer or field delivery.
  • Expert-level coding ability in JavaScript and one or more additional languages (Java, Python, or equivalent), with a proven track record of shipping and scaling production systems.
  • Deep experience deploying and integrating AI features and GenAI models, including Now Assist, AI Agents, or equivalent platforms, across multiple customer environments and deployment patterns.
  • Strong judgment on prompt engineering and non-deterministic model behavior, including the ability to advise on reliability, production readiness, and edge cases.
  • A strategic mindset about standards, tooling, and scalability — you balance pragmatism with the long-term health of the program.
  • Proven ability to build, own, and scale shared infrastructure and platforms that multiple teams depend on.
  • Strong mentoring and coaching capability — you actively develop the engineers around you and leave them better than you found them.
  • Excellent communication and presence across technical and non-technical audiences, including customer executives and internal leadership.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and drive change at a program or organizational level without formal authority.

This will include helping in aligning new use cases to the CISO goals, and identify growth opportunities by informing the customer of our latest innovations, capabilities, and products and match these to the clients’ business goals.   • Act as the customer advocate within Armis, coordinating across teams to meet customer objectives.

  • Ensure deployment and configuration align with key business use cases and are delivered on schedule.

  • Stay current on third-party integrations and how they interact with Armis within customer environments.

  • Serve as a subject matter expert in your area of technical proficiency.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Support, and Sales teams to drive account success.

Knowledge of healthcare/ICT devices, manufacturers, or applications.

Experience securing IT, IoT, or healthcare systems.

Job Description

About the team

The Conversational AI team at ServiceNow builds the core platform behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI experience. We are a group of applied scientists and software engineers working at the intersection of research and production. Our work spans the full stack that makes Otto capable: agent orchestration, including harness engineering, prompt tuning, agent skills, policy design, and quality evaluation across languages; the A2A and MCP protocols that let agents collaborate and connect to tools; background channels and conversational triggers that bring agents into action; AI-native licensing and pricing; and the central caching layer that connects the ServiceNow platform to the services powering Otto.

We are seeking a Staff AI-Native DevOps Engineer to join a new DevOps practice within the Conversational AI team. You will own the build, deployment, and reliability of the systems behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI platform, from commit through production across our SaaS environments. You will manage senior-level technical consultants and Business Process Consultants (BPCs) to deliver transformative solutions while driving key strategic initiatives. You will be instrumental in expanding the ServiceNow Security and Risk footprint, ensuring delivery excellence, nurturing deep customer relationships, and maximizing customer value realization in the security and risk domain.

  • Proven ability to consult, influence, and establish credibility with executive-level stakeholders, including CISOs, Chief Risk Officers, Chief Compliance Officers, CIOs, and other business leaders. 
  • Exceptional people leadership skills, including coaching, mentoring, and talent development of technical and consulting teams.

  • Dedication to customer success, delivery excellence, and continuous improvement.

Job Description

Team & Role: 

Moveworks is looking for a mixed-methods Principal Experience Researcher, AI to turn complex user behavior into clear, actionable product direction. You’ll combine qualitative research with quantitative analysis to understand not only what people do, but why they do it.
You’ll serve as a critical bridge between end-user experiences and the machine learning systems that power them. By translating user needs, behaviors, and feedback into measurable signals, you’ll help teams evaluate and improve model performance—and ensure our AI creates experiences that are useful, trustworthy, and intuitive.
This is a generalist research role for someone comfortable working across methods and stages of product development. You don’t need an engineering background, but you should be curious about how AI systems work and able to collaborate effectively with technical partners.
 

What you get to do in this role 

  • Identify and prioritize opportunities across the end-user journey by connecting large-scale behavioral data with qualitative insights, shaping product strategy and roadmap priorities.
  • Set research strategy and prioritize the research portfolio around high-impact user and business questions, selecting approaches that balance scope, depth, speed, and confidence to guide investment decisions.
  • Translate user needs and behaviors into clear signals that inform the design, development, and evaluation of AI and machine learning systems.
  • Define the evaluation strategy for AI-powered experiences, establishing frameworks, quality standards, and shared success measures across product, design, and machine learning teams that connect model performance to usability, relevance, trust, and user outcomes.
  • Investigate model and experience failures, identify recurring patterns, and recommend improvements across the product and underlying systems.
  • Serve as a strategic partner to product, design, engineering, data science, and machine learning leaders, framing critical questions, challenging assumptions, and aligning teams on evidence-based product direction.
  • Evaluate new concepts and product experiences throughout development—from early discovery and prototyping through launch and continuous improvement.
  • Communicate findings through clear narratives, data visualizations, research artifacts, and recommendations tailored to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Qualifications

What You Bring:  

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • 10+ years of professional experience in user experience research, product research, human-computer interaction, behavioral science, or a related field.
  • Strong grounding in qualitative and quantitative research methods, including generative and evaluative approaches, with sound judgment in sampling, survey design, experimentation, bias, validity, and data interpretation.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze large or complex behavioral datasets, including product usage logs, and translate findings into actionable product insights.
  • Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, including the ability to make complex findings clear to different audiences.
  • Strong collaboration and stakeholder-management skills, with experience building alignment across product managers, engineers, and designers.
  • A portfolio or work samples that demonstrate your research process, analytical capabilities, and influence on product decisions and user outcomes.

The nice to have:  

  • Experience conducting lean UX research in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience researching AI-powered, machine learning, conversational, search, or recommendation experiences.
  • Experience developing or improving evaluation systems, benchmarks, rubrics, or quality metrics for AI products.
  • Familiarity with product analytics, experimentation platforms, data visualization tools, or statistical analysis software.
  • Experience using SQL, R, Python, or similar tools. Technical fluency is valued, but hands-on programming experience is not required.

This role is part of our Product Design team, which turns a deep understanding of our users and customers into product experiences they love. At ServiceNow, design has an intentional seat at the table, and we partner with Engineering and Product Management from the outset. 

We're looking for a Senior Director of Product Creative Direction to define and evolve the visual expression of our product portfolio. This leader will set a distinctive product visual direction, translate it into a scalable system, and help teams make complex enterprise software feel clear, coherent, modern, and unmistakably ServiceNow. 

This is a product-focused creative leadership role. You will work as part of cross-functional software development teams and partner across Platform and the business units to connect creative vision with customer needs, product strategy, and technical realities. Product teams retain ownership of their product strategy, design, roadmap, quality, and delivery; this role provides shared visual direction, systems, critique, and enablement. 

You will also advance the responsible use of AI in creative work and make accessibility intrinsic to the product visual language. 

What you get to do in this role 

  • Define and champion a differentiated visual direction for the product portfolio, grounded in our brand, customer needs, product strategy, and the evolving relationship between people and AI. 

  • Establish a clear point of view across typography, color, composition, iconography, illustration, motion, data visualization, density, and other visual foundations. 

  • Create future-state concepts, reference experiences, and exemplars that make the visual direction tangible. 

  • Work with Design Systems, Product Design, Content Design, Accessibility, Localization, and Research to translate the visual language into scalable foundations, components, patterns, and guidance. 

  • Partner with Design Systems, Product Management and Engineering throughout the software development lifecycle so the creative direction can be applied effectively in shipped products. 

  • Define where consistency is essential, where variation creates value, and how teams can extend the system without creating a centralized bottleneck. 

  • Lead the strategy for AI-enabled creative exploration, prototyping, asset creation, system evolution, and evaluation, focusing on meaningful gains in range, speed, consistency, and quality. 

  • Move promising AI approaches from experimentation to repeatable practice through pilots, playbooks, training, exemplars, responsible-use standards, and measurable adoption goals. 

  • Provide creative direction and hands-on critique for priority, cross-product initiatives while reinforcing product-team ownership. 

  • Partner with Brand and Marketing so the company expression and product experience tell a coherent story while remaining useful and native to interactive software. 

  • Make accessibility intrinsic to the creative vision and visual foundations, partnering with Accessibility and Engineering to meet or exceed applicable standards, including WCAG 2.2 AA. 

  • Lead, develop, and attract exceptional visual, motion, and multidisciplinary design talent. 

  • Build the culture, enablement, and shared critique practices that help product designers and distributed visual designers understand, apply, and continually raise the visual craft bar. 

  • Build a network of creative leaders and contributors across the business units who can extend the direction while maintaining coherence. 

Qualifications

Preferred Qualifications 

  • 12+ years of experience in product design, visual design, experience design, creative direction, or a related field, including significant leadership experience shipping complex digital products. 

  • A portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft and creative leadership across shipped product experiences, not only brand campaigns or marketing communications. 

  • Experience defining or materially evolving a visual language across a complex, multi-product software portfolio. 

  • Deep understanding of design systems, including visual foundations, design tokens, components, patterns, governance, contribution models, and the relationship between design and code. 

  • Demonstrated experience adopting AI-enabled creative tools and workflows and moving teams from isolated experimentation to sustained, responsible use at scale. 

  • Proven ability to influence senior executives and align multiple organizations without relying solely on reporting authority. 

  • Expert command of typography, color, composition, interaction, motion, and information hierarchy, with the judgment to apply them to dense and complex product workflows. 

  • Strong systems thinking and the ability to connect an inspiring creative idea to the practices and adoption mechanisms required to make it real at scale. 

  • Demonstrated commitment to accessible and inclusive design, with working knowledge of WCAG and platform accessibility considerations. 

  • Excellent communication, storytelling, facilitation, and critique skills, including the ability to make a direction compelling to executives and actionable for delivery teams.

  • Experience participating in the complete product development lifecycle of web and/or software applications.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Position overview 

ServiceNow is seeking a Senior Director of Site Reliability Engineering to build and lead a world-class SRE organization across our observability and control plane product portfolios. You will architect reliability programs that span internal platforms and commercial products, establishing SRE culture, practices, and tooling from the ground up. 

This is a program-building role. You will define SRE strategy, set operational standards, build teams (starting from scratch or scaling existing pockets), and drive measurable people and organizational transformation. You will report to the VP of Engineering and partner with product, platform, and infrastructure leaders across multiple business units. 

Key responsibilities 

Program building & strategy 

  • Build an SRE program from the ground up—define charter, operating model, hiring strategy, and multi-year roadmap 

  • Establish SRE principles, practices, and standards across observability products (OODP, metrics, alerting) and control plane offerings 

  • Create unified reliability frameworks that work for both internal-facing and customer-facing systems 

  • Design SRE on-call rotations, incident response processes, and blameless postmortem culture 

Team leadership & people transformation 

  • Build and scale an SRE team from existing base across observability and control plane domains 

  • Design hiring criteria and interview processes that attract high-caliber SREs with platform and reliability expertise 

  • Create mentorship and career development paths; foster SRE culture and continuous learning 

  • Drive organizational transformation: shift product and infrastructure teams toward reliability-first mindsets 

  • Establish clear SRE career levels, expectations, and growth frameworks 

Reliability & operational excellence 

  • Define SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets for observability and control plane products; operationalize them 

  • Build AI native toil reduction initiatives; automate repetitive operational work across SRE and product teams 

  • Own incident management: design escalation policies, postmortem practices, and continuous improvement loops 

  • Partner with platform/infrastructure teams to improve reliability infrastructure (CI/CD, deployment systems, monitoring) 

  • Establish reliability metrics, dashboards, and reporting for leadership visibility 

Cross-functional alignment 

  • Partner with product teams to embed SRE thinking in design and development of new features 

  • Work with observability leadership on internal vs. commercial product strategy—tailor SRE programs accordingly 

  • Collaborate with customer success and support on customer-facing reliability; define SLA/SLO communication 

  • Partner with infrastructure and platform teams on shared services, runbooks, and operational tooling 

  • Engage with security and compliance on reliability-related governance and risk 

Qualifications

Required qualifications 

  • 12+ years of experience in SRE, platform engineering, or reliability engineering at scale 

  • 5+ years in leadership roles (director or principal engineer) managing SRE or reliability teams of 10+ engineers 

  • Demonstrated track record building SRE programs from scratch or scaling immature programs—with measurable business impact 

  • Strong evidence of driving people and organizational transformation; ability to shift culture from reactive to proactive reliability 

  • Deep expertise in SRE practices: SLOs, error budgets, blameless postmortems, on-call design, toil reduction 

  • Hands-on experience with observability platforms (metrics, logging, tracing, alerting) 

  • Experience operating both internal platforms and commercial products (SaaS) 

  • Comfort with the messy reality of multi-team, multi-product environments—ability to establish standards and drive adoption 

Preferred qualifications 

  • Experience with control plane architectures or platform-as-a-service systems 

  • Background building SRE programs in hybrid or multi-cloud deployments 

  • Track record of mentoring and developing other SRE/platform leaders 

  • Familiarity with chaos engineering, reliability testing, or resilience frameworks 

  • Open-source contribution or thought leadership in SRE community 

Core competencies 

Program building 

  • Ability to define a charter, secure stakeholder buy-in, and execute a multi-year strategy from concept to maturity 

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and building in greenfield environments 

People transformation 

  • Proven ability to shift organizational mindsets—making reliability a shared responsibility, not just an SRE function 

  • Strong coaching and mentorship instincts; creates environments where people grow 

  • Excellent communication skills—able to articulate reliability concepts to engineers, product managers, and executives 

Technical depth 

  • Hands-on SRE expertise; can code, debug, and architect solutions alongside the team 

  • Deep understanding of observability, monitoring, and telemetry infrastructure 

  • Familiarity with multiple deployment models, cloud platforms, and operational challenges 

Operational leadership 

  • Data-driven decision making; comfortable with SLOs, metrics, and evidence-based practices 

  • Cross-functional influencing; ability to drive change without direct authority 

  • Bias toward action and iteration—comfort making decisions with incomplete information 

What we offer 

  • Competitive salary and equity package 

  • Comprehensive health, wellness, and retirement benefits 

  • Unlimited PTO and flexible work arrangements 

  • Leadership coaching and executive development 

  • The opportunity to build a world-class SRE organization and shape reliability culture across critical product lines

Job Description

Please Note: 

Due to Government of Canada regulatory requirements, this position requires the successful completion of a Government of Canada Reliability Status screening as a condition of employment. The screening process requires 5 years of verifiable background history. This includes identity verification, education verification, a criminal record check, and a credit check. Candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain Reliability Status, which generally requires Canadian citizenship or Canadian permanent resident status.  Employment is contingent upon successful completion and maintenance of the required screening.

About the Team

The ServiceNow SRE team is a group of highly technical engineers responsible for maintaining and improving the reliability, scalability, and performance of ServiceNow's cloud infrastructure. You'll design and operate cloud-native platforms for software validation, release validation, and production readiness, and partner with globally distributed engineering teams.

The Role

As a Staff SRE, you'll set the technical direction for reliability and release quality across multiple teams. You'll build the platforms and automation that let engineers ship safely at scale, shape architecture decisions, and raise the bar for operational excellence through hands-on work and mentorship.

What you get to do in this role:

  • Design, build, and operate cloud-native engineering platforms for software validation, release validation, and production readiness.
  • Design and maintain production-like release and test environments.
  • Build automated test pipelines, observability, and quality gates into CI/CD workflows.
  • Reduce manual toil through automation and shift-left practices.
  • Build reusable frameworks, self-service environments, test data management, and mock services.
  • Design and enhance Kubernetes-based platforms for test infrastructure, release automation, and developer self-service.
  • Implement automated checks for failure detection, deployment verification, policy enforcement, security, and resilience.
  • Resolve complex platform, infrastructure, and networking challenges.
  • Lead architecture reviews and design discussions, and drive projects independently across teams.
  • Mentor engineers through code reviews, guidance, and knowledge sharing.
  • Promote a culture of reliability, automation, and operational excellence.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • 8+ years of experience in SRE, DevOps, platform, software, or infrastructure engineering, with a Bachelor's degree or 6 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years experience; or equivalent experience.
  • Hands-on Kubernetes experience across cluster operations, networking, storage, security, autoscaling, and multi-cluster environments.
  • Experience building and operating highly available cloud-native platforms.
  • Experience integrating Kubernetes with CI/CD, GitOps, automated test pipelines, and deployment validation.
  • Experience with progressive delivery, including canary deployments, feature flags, and automated rollback.
  • Experience with chaos engineering, resilience testing, and disaster recovery.
  • Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Java, or Ruby.
  • Solid understanding of observability, SLIs/SLOs, incident management, and distributed systems operations.
  • Ability to drive projects independently and thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, with a strong ownership mindset.
  • Experience integrating AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Observability and monitoring platforms at scale, including Grafana and VictoriaMetrics.
  • DevOps and GitOps tools such as GitLab CI/CD, Argo CD, or Flux.
  • Test automation frameworks such as Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, REST Assured, PyTest, or JUnit/TestNG.
  • Test orchestration, flaky test detection, and test data management.
  • Service virtualization, contract testing, and synthetic testing.
  • Infrastructure as Code with Terraform or Ansible.
  • Kubernetes ecosystem tools such as Helm, Istio/Linkerd, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry.
  • Managed Kubernetes on AWS (EKS), Azure (AKS), or Google Cloud (GKE).
  • AI-assisted engineering, intelligent testing, or operational automation.

title: Senior Reliability Engineer - Veza
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Veza is the pioneer in identity security, purpose-built to answer the fundamental question enterprises face: who can and should take what action on what data. Veza's Access Graph platform maps an organization's entire identity ecosystem across users, groups, roles, policies, permissions, and resources—providing deep visibility and control over human, non-human, and agentic identities across SaaS, cloud, on-prem, and custom applications. With over 30 billion access permissions under management, global enterprises including Blackstone, Expedia, and Wynn Resorts trust Veza to manage privileged access monitoring, non-human identity security, access entitlement management, and next-generation identity governance.

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Veza is now part of the ServiceNow family, with the acquisition closing in March 2026. The combination brings together Veza's AI-native Access Graph with ServiceNow's AI Control Tower and agentic workflows, enabling organizations to enforce end-to-end identity security rooted in the principle of least privilege across applications, data, cloud environments, and AI agents. Job Description

The Machine Learning Developer designs, builds, ships, and operates applications whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored. The Developer builds the engine behind ServiceNow's optimization products — the algorithms and pipelines that turn sophisticated scheduling and resource-allocation problems into fast, reliable customer outcomes. The work is evolving — where "AI-driven" once meant applying ML techniques to optimization problems, it now also means using AI agents as part of the build process itself. This role expects both: someone who can design an efficient algorithm from scratch, and someone who can specify a problem precisely enough to direct an AI agent to implement part of it, then verify the result is correct. The developer owns the correctness, performance, and robustness of what ships, regardless of whether a human or an agent wrote it.

What you get to do:

  • Build Optimization applications. Design, build and operate applications built around advanced optimization models in production at scale. This includes API design, data ingestion, multiprocessing, observability, advanced algorithm development, performance benchmarking, and automated testing. 
  • Build automated evaluation and test model behaviour. Design and operate the evaluation system that supports development and delivering features with confidence.  
  • Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents. Convert requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and review agent output for correctness and maintainability. Contribute to teams AI-harness helping shape the way agents are leveraged. 
  • Own quality, safety, and reliability in production. Manage deployments, monitor service availability, implement alerting and respond to customer issues before they even know they have a problem. 
  • Deliver as a forward deployed engineer. Work closely with customers when the work calls for it. Understanding business requirements and product capabilities to help customers get to value faster and use learnings to influence product roadmap. 
  • Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, designers, conversation designers, and engineers to define success criteria, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly. 

Qualifications

  • Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of OOP, data structures, algorithms, system design, concurrency, parallelism, APIs, data modeling, and testing. 
  • Experience with key Technologies: Experience with Python is strongly preferred; experience in Java, JavaScript, Kubernetes, or GraphQL is a bonus. 
  • Python, MLflow, Weights & Biases, LoRA, PEFT, SageMaker, Vertex AI, AzureML, Kubeflow, Airflow, Prefect, TorchServe, Triton, vLLM, SHAP, LIME, pandas, Spark, SQL
  • Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers under incomplete information and fixed timelines, judgment about when a fast local solution is right and when to hold out for the durable one, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers. 
  • Experience with mission critical systems. Demonstrated experience developing reliable and resilient systems. 
  • AI Native Approach. Strong critical thinking and a track record of integrating AI into engineering processes, SDLC, workflows, or decision making. 
  • Domain expertise. Familiarity with Operations Research, Vehicle Routing Problems, Mathematical Optimization, Field Service Management is a plus but not required

descriptionHtml:

Job Description

 What you get to do in this role:

The senior technical architect, infrastructure and cloud sets direction for how our corporate and cloud infrastructure evolves to support secure, reliable, scalable, and cost-effective business services. As part of the technical architecture team, this role connects infrastructure and cloud decisions to enterprise architecture and the broader technology roadmap. The role researches new technologies, advises on current solutions, and drives improvement, including upgrades, retirements, and replacements. This is a senior individual contributor role that sets direction through standards, roadmaps, guardrails, and architecture decisions. You will not run day-to-day operations or build infrastructure yourself. You will make sure the teams that do have a coherent target architecture, practical guardrails, and a clear path from where we are to where we need to be. 

Scope 

This role advises on and supports infrastructure and cloud architecture for technologies outside the ServiceNow platform: data centers, public and hybrid cloud, compute, storage, networking and connectivity, backup and recovery, and the infrastructure dependencies of corporate systems. Other teams continue to own the systems they run. This role works with them to shape direction, standards, and decisions. 

This role does not cover ServiceNow platform instance architecture or configuration, or AI and data architecture, although it does support the infrastructure that AI and data workloads run on. Enterprise security architecture sits with the security architecture team. You will partner with that team closely, as a peer stakeholder in architecture forums. 

What you will own 

  • Help define the current-state, transition-state, and target-state infrastructure and cloud architecture, with a multiyear roadmap tied to business priorities, risk, lifecycle, capacity, and cost. Help align that direction with enterprise architecture principles and the broader technology roadmap, and surface dependencies that affect enterprise plans. 

  • Establish reference architectures, principles, standards, and patterns across cloud, data center, networking, compute, storage, containers, and backup. Advise on infrastructure as code and policy as code, and support delivery teams in adopting them. 

  • Help define cloud governance, standards, and architectural guardrails for Azure and GCP, including account and subscription structure, landing zones, cost controls, and policy as code. Advise teams on operating within them, and surface where a guardrail needs to change. 

  • Lead infrastructure architecture reviews and provide architecture input on major technical decisions. Help scope proofs of concept and vendor evaluations. Evaluate options, document tradeoffs, risks, and value, fit, operability, and total cost, and help drive decisions to closure with accountable stakeholders. 

  • Recommend resilience and compliance requirements for high availability, disaster recovery, backup and recovery, and continuity, and help align recovery objectives with business criticality. 

  • Partner with Security Architecture on resilience, compliance, and zero-trust, so that security requirements are built into infrastructure and cloud standards from the start. 

  • Look ahead to AI and ML infrastructure needs, including compute capacity, specialized hardware, data storage, and hybrid hosting. Understand the agentic AI patterns, such as RAG, A2A, and MCP, that shape those needs. Research emerging technologies that could change how we build and run infrastructure, and advise on when to adopt them. 

  • Default to out-of-the-box capabilities. Recommend a documented case for any custom pattern or exception and advise on retiring custom solutions where a standard capability will do. 

  • Support and collaborate regularly with the DT Integration, Core Systems, and Product teams to align infrastructure needs, dependencies, and roadmaps. Advise these teams on the infrastructure implications of their integration, core system, and product decisions, and help plan changes that depend on shared infrastructure. 

  • Partner with finance and operations to inform infrastructure economics through capacity planning, lifecycle management, workload placement, and FinOps practices. Draw on incidents, capacity trends, audit findings, and resilience test results to inform standards and roadmaps. 

  • Represent infrastructure and cloud in the architecture team and its governance forums, including the Architecture Review Board. Build trusted relationships with senior technology and business leaders, and mentor architects and engineers. 

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in infrastructure, cloud, platform engineering, or systems engineering, including substantial architecture responsibility for complex enterprise environments. 

  • Demonstrated success defining infrastructure and cloud strategy and roadmaps that span multiple technology domains and delivery teams. 

  • Deep expertise in several infrastructure domains, with enough breadth to make integrated decisions across cloud, network, compute, storage, resilience, and cost. 

  • Strong working knowledge of Azure and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) architecture, including landing zones, connectivity, identity dependencies, workload placement, and shared-responsibility models. 

  • Solid understanding of agentic AI concepts and patterns, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent-to-agent (A2A) communication, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and related technologies. 

  • Experience integrating disparate systems, with a strong understanding of enterprise integration patterns, such as APIs, messaging, and event-driven architecture. 

  • Experience defining cloud governance, guardrails, and standards in a large enterprise, and getting teams to adopt them. 

  • Experience creating and governing reference architectures, standards, and architecture decision records. 

  • Working knowledge of infrastructure as code and modern automation practices. 

  • Ability to evaluate architecture choices on business value, risk, cost, and operational evidence, not technology preference. 

  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and technical teams without relying on direct authority. 

  • Clear written and verbal communication for both engineering and executive audiences. 

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience. 

Preferred qualifications 

  • Experience in a large, global, regulated, or mission-critical environment. 

  • Familiarity with IT service management practices, including the IT Infrastructure Library (ITIL), and with configuration management database (CMDB) alignment for infrastructure configuration items. 

  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture frameworks, such as TOGAF or COBIT, or equivalent. 

  • Experience with release planning using Agile and Scrum practices. 

  • Familiarity with AI and ML infrastructure requirements, such as GPU and accelerator capacity, and with zero-trust architecture. 

  • Experience with FinOps, technology portfolio management, and infrastructure cost modeling. 

  • Relevant architecture, cloud, networking, security, or infrastructure certifications. 

  • Experience guiding vendor strategy or major platform selection.
