Job Description

As a Sales Coach, you will work one on one with sellers to lift pipeline generation, deal quality, and forecast accuracy. This is a hands-on field coaching role. You will spend most of your week with sellers and in live deal work, and the rest building the programs that scale what works. You report to the manager of the department and partner closely with frontline sales managers, enablement, product marketing, and the teams integrating newly acquired sellers.

What you get to do in this role:

Coach sellers one on one - This is the center of the role. You will spend most of your week with individual sellers, working on whatever stands between them and their number.

● Run a recurring one-on-one coaching cadence with each assigned seller against a written individual development plan

● Coach the full seller motion—prospecting and outbound rigor, territory and account management, deal management and qualification, executive presence, time and calendar management, CRM accuracy and forecast hygiene, and personal change management through reorgs and portfolio shifts

● Facilitate role plays and certification checkpoints across discovery, executive conversations, pricing, objection handling, and competitive positioning, so mastery is demonstrated rather than assumed

● Observe live customer calls and give same-day feedback that names the specific behavior to change

Build coaching programs with your manager

● Partner with your manager to design programs that answer real business needs—segment ramp paths, focused skill sprints, manager coaching enablement, and remediation tracks

● Build segment-appropriate variants where Enterprise and Commercial need different treatment of the same skill—multi-stakeholder pursuit strategy and executive alignment on one side, call volume, cycle discipline, and portfolio juggling on the other

● Design coaching that scales across a large Commercial population without losing the personal quality that makes coaching work

● Contribute reusable assets back to the global library: playbooks, call frameworks, role play scenarios, and certification rubrics

● Pilot, measure, and retire—keep what moves the number and cut what does not

Support large-scale training events

● Help design and deliver org-wide moments: sales kickoff, bootcamps, mid-year kickoffs, product launch enablement, and field readiness days

● Own assigned tracks end to end—content, facilitators, breakout design, certification, and the reinforcement plan that follows

● Build the follow-through so event content shows up in seller behavior 30 and 60 days later

Document and report progress

● Build and maintain the documentation layer that makes coaching visible and auditable—rep scorecards, skill matrices, certification records, development plans, and progress over time

● Report coaching impact to sales and enablement leadership on a set cadence, tied to business results rather than activity counts

● Keep records consistent enough that another coach could pick up any rep and know exactly where they stand

Shorten time to productivity for new hires, transfers, and acquired teams

● Own the coaching side of ramp for new hires, internal transfers, and sellers joining through acquisition, with an explicit goal of moving time to productivity from roughly six months to three

● Build and run acquisition-specific enablement: cross-portfolio positioning, joint account mapping, tooling and process conversion, and the cultural onboarding that makes acquired sellers feel like part of the team quickly

● Track ramp milestones by cohort and flag an at-risk ramp early enough to fix it

● Give hiring managers a clear read on where each new seller stands and what they need next

Validate readiness on new products, releases, and acquisitions

● Assess whether sellers are genuinely equipped to sell new products, new releases, and newly acquired portfolios—measured through certification, call review, and pipeline evidence, not attendance

● Report readiness gaps to product, marketing, and enablement partners with a recommended fix and a date

● Re-test after remediation and close the loop

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

● Seven or more years in enterprise or commercial software sales, sales management, or sales coaching and enablement

● Direct experience with both a large-deal Enterprise motion and a higher-velocity Commercial or mid-market motion, and a clear point of view on how coaching differs between them

● A track record of coaching adults to behavior change—specific sellers or teams who improved on a measurable metric because of your work

● Fluency in at least one recognized sales methodology, such as MEDDICC, Challenger, Strategic Selling, or Command of the Message, and the ability to coach to it rather than just describe it

● Strong CRM discipline—you can inspect a pipeline and tell the difference between a data problem and a deal problem

● Comfort with the enablement stack: CRM, conversation intelligence, sales content management, and a learning management system

● Credibility with senior sellers and frontline managers—this role carries influence, not authority

● Excellent facilitation and written communication skills, and the judgment to know when to teach and when to ask

Nice to Have:

● Prior quota-carrying experience at both Enterprise and Commercial

● Experience coaching across a multi-product or platform portfolio

● Formal coaching certification, such as ICF or equivalent

● Experience integrating an acquired sales team

Build coaching programs with your manager

● Partner with your manager to design programs that answer real business needs—segment ramp paths, focused skill sprints, manager coaching enablement, and remediation tracks

● Build segment-appropriate variants where Enterprise and Commercial need different treatment of the same skill—multi-stakeholder pursuit strategy and executive alignment on one side, call volume, cycle discipline, and portfolio juggling on the other

● Design coaching that scales across a large Commercial population without losing the personal quality that makes coaching work

● Contribute reusable assets back to the global library: playbooks, call frameworks, role play scenarios, and certification rubrics

● Pilot, measure, and retire—keep what moves the number and cut what does not

Support large-scale training events

● Help design and deliver org-wide moments: sales kickoff, bootcamps, mid-year kickoffs, product launch enablement, and field readiness days

● Own assigned tracks end to end—content, facilitators, breakout design, certification, and the reinforcement plan that follows

● Build the follow-through so event content shows up in seller behavior 30 and 60 days later

Document and report progress

● Build and maintain the documentation layer that makes coaching visible and auditable—rep scorecards, skill matrices, certification records, development plans, and progress over time

● Report coaching impact to sales and enablement leadership on a set cadence, tied to business results rather than activity counts

● Keep records consistent enough that another coach could pick up any rep and know exactly where they stand

● Own the coaching side of ramp for new hires, internal transfers, and sellers joining through acquisition, with an explicit goal of moving time to productivity from roughly six months to three

● Build and run acquisition-specific enablement: cross-portfolio positioning, joint account mapping, tooling and process conversion, and the cultural onboarding that makes acquired sellers feel like part of the team quickly

● Track ramp milestones by cohort and flag an at-risk ramp early enough to fix it

● Give hiring managers a clear read on where each new seller stands and what they need next

Validate readiness on new products, releases, and acquisitions

● Assess whether sellers are genuinely equipped to sell new products, new releases, and newly acquired portfolios—measured through certification, call review, and pipeline evidence, not attendance

● Report readiness gaps to product, marketing, and enablement partners with a recommended fix and a date

● Re-test after remediation and close the loop

● Seven or more years in enterprise or commercial software sales, sales management, or sales coaching and enablement

● Direct experience with both a large-deal Enterprise motion and a higher-velocity Commercial or mid-market motion, and a clear point of view on how coaching differs between them

● A track record of coaching adults to behavior change—specific sellers or teams who improved on a measurable metric because of your work

● Fluency in at least one recognized sales methodology, such as MEDDICC, Challenger, Strategic Selling, or Command of the Message, and the ability to coach to it rather than just describe it

● Strong CRM discipline—you can inspect a pipeline and tell the difference between a data problem and a deal problem

● Comfort with the enablement stack: CRM, conversation intelligence, sales content management, and a learning management system

● Credibility with senior sellers and frontline managers—this role carries influence, not authority

● Excellent facilitation and written communication skills, and the judgment to know when to teach and when to ask

● Prior quota-carrying experience at both Enterprise and Commercial

● Experience coaching across a multi-product or platform portfolio

This is a hands-on IC4 team lead: an analytical operator who sets direction for a small pod of partner operations analysts, raises the bar on rigor, and leads with an AI-first mindset — using AI and automation to simplify how the business runs, eliminate manual work, and give leadership faster, more reliable insight. 

Run the Business: Forecasting & Operating Rhythm 

  • Own the partner business forecast — weekly and quarterly by GEO and stage (Commit / Expect / Upside / Pre-Pipeline), with call accuracy tracked and variance explained 

  • Design and run the operating cadence: weekly business reviews, pipeline inspections, quarter-end readiness, and QBR packages for partner and executive audiences 

  • Define and own the KPI framework and scorecards for partner performance — consumption, burndown, pipeline coverage, and partner health — anchored on a single source of truth 

  • Surface trends, risks, and opportunities proactively with a point of view and recommended action, before they become escalations 

Pre-Buy Program Ownership 

  • Own end-to-end Pre-Buy execution across both active contracts as reviewer and approver (not processor) of inventory tracking, burndown, OPTY validation, add-backs, swaps, and leftover reconciliation 

  • Deliver bridge-normalized burndown reporting and flag slow-burn patterns, stranded inventory, and expiration risk early 

  • Own LOI governance: interpret contract language into booking and comp guidance, and prevent LOI actions from triggering unintended downsell or GRR distortion 

Process, Policy & Governance 

  • Build robust, documented processes for partner deal intake, approvals, exceptions, and reconciliation — designed to scale with volume, not headcount 

  • Author and maintain partner operations policy (crediting, exceptions, program rules) with Finance, Deal Desk, Legal, Revenue Operations, and Comp, and drive clean adoption across the field 

  • Uphold governance and controls: approval audit trails, policy compliance, and decision logs that stand up to Finance and audit scrutiny 

  • Run continuous improvement — find the root cause of recurring escalations and retire them through process, policy, or system fixes 

Strategic Business Partner to Sales 

  • Act as the operational thought partner to GPLs, GPMs, and Partner Sales leaders — removing deal blockers, resolving policy gray areas, and accelerating pipeline through the right partner motions 

  • Serve as the first escalation point for field issues — mis-bookings, comp disputes, exceptions — resolving directly or packaging for leadership with a clear recommendation 

  • Own field and partner enablement: playbooks, SOPs, and self-serve reference materials that reduce recurring questions and speed deal execution 

  • Contribute to annual planning — partner targets, coverage inputs, and investment cases grounded in data 

AI-Led Simplification & Scale 

  • Lead the team's AI agenda: identify high-volume manual work (reporting, reconciliation, intake triage, policy Q&A) and redesign it with AI, agents, and automation 

  • Build and deploy AI-enabled tools — automated forecast and burndown reporting, anomaly detection on inventory and bookings, and assistants that answer policy and process questions for the field 

  • Set data quality and governance standards for AI use: human-in-the-loop review, accuracy checks, and responsible handling of partner and deal data 

  • Measure and communicate impact — hours returned, cycle-time reduction, forecast accuracy — and scale wins across Global Partner Operations 

Team Leadership 

  • Provide day-to-day leadership for a small pod of partner operations analysts — set priorities, review work quality, and coach for ownership and judgment 

  • Build the team's analytical and AI fluency through shared tooling, templates, and peer review 

  • Model calm urgency at quarter-end and serve as backup to the Director on partner operations decisions 

Qualifications

Required Qualification

  • 6+ years in Partner Operations, Sales or GTM Operations, Business Operations, or Sales Strategy in global enterprise SaaS 

  • Strong analytical background: forecasting, pipeline analytics, and KPI design, with advanced Excel/BI and SQL or equivalent data skills 

  • Demonstrated, hands-on use of AI to simplify or automate business workflows — GenAI assistants, agent workflows, or automation that removed manual effort at measurable scale 

  • Track record designing and enforcing process, policy, and governance in a cross-functional environment 

  • Experience leading, mentoring, or setting direction for analysts or project teams 

  • Experience working with or within a large GSI or strategic channel partner — understands how GSIs structure deals, allocate budgets, and consume licenses 

  • Comfort with enterprise SaaS deal mechanics: NNACV/ACV, GRR/NRR, revenue bridge normalization, crediting, and comp treatment 

  • Proven strategic partner to sales leaders, influencing across Finance, Legal, Deal Desk, Revenue Operations, and Comp without direct authority 

  • Executive communication: turns complex data into clear narratives and recommendations 

  • Operates with calm urgency in high-stakes, quarter-end environments with competing priorities

  • Prior experience supporting a large GSI relationship (Cognizant, Infosys, or similar) at global scale 

  • Proficiency with Salesforce, Power BI, SQL, and Python or low-code automation platforms

Job Description

Team

Platform Security builds foundational security infrastructure and AI-driven detection systems for enterprise-scale operations. Our mission is to make security proactive, intelligent, and seamlessly integrated into the ServiceNow platform. Cryptography within Platform Security owns the cryptographic backbone of the ServiceNow platform across multiple domains: certificate lifecycle, key management, secrets distribution, and workload identity for a SaaS platform. This is core, regulated-environment security engineering

Role Summary 

As a Staff AI Security & Crypto Engineer, you will architect and deliver enterprise-scale security solutions that integrate cryptographic systems with machine learning, reasoning engines, and real-time inference. You will bring deep expertise in applied cryptography, strong technical leadership, and hands-on machine learning depth — designing and operating intelligent, adaptive security systems for key management, PKI, and secrets infrastructure at SaaS scale.

What you get to do in this role :

  • Design, build, and maintain high-quality, scalable, secure cryptographic services meeting FIPS compliance and regulated-environment requirements
  • Architect and operate mission-critical crypto services  with reliability and security as first-class design constraints
  • Own services end-to-end on Kubernetes in a multi-tenant SaaS environment - deployment, scaling, on-call, incident response
  • Bring a security mindset to every design review: threat model the feature, not just the happy path — this is a deliberate area we're leveling up as a team
  • Evaluate where AI/ML has a legitimate role in the crypto/security space — anomaly detection in key usage, ML-assisted certificate lifecycle risk scoring, AI-assisted code review for cryptographic anti-patterns — and separate that from where it's a distraction
  • Collaborate with product owners, security architects, and platform teams to translate compliance and security requirements into working cryptographic frameworks
  • Mentor engineers on secure coding, cryptographic pitfalls, and design review rigor
  • Stay current on cryptographic advancements, including post-quantum readiness, and bring that forward before it's a compliance deadline

Qualifications

Preferred qualifications :

  • Direct experience in cryptography, PKI, key management, or secrets management — certificate lifecycle systems, HSM/KMS integration, or crypto-agility work
  • Some hands-on AI/ML exposure — not a research background, but real experience applying ML techniques to security/ops problems (anomaly detection, risk scoring, log/telemetry analysis) or critically integrating LLM tooling into engineering workflows
  • Experience with regulated environments (FIPS 140-2/3, FedRAMP, common criteria, or similar)
  • Exposure to post-quantum cryptography
  • Track record mentoring engineers and raising the security bar on a team, not just shipping features

Basic qualifications :

  • 8+ years of experience in professional software engineering experience; Java, Go, or a comparable strongly-typed language at production scale
  • Strong CS fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, OO design, distributed systems tradeoffs
  • Production experience running services on Kubernetes (deployments, Helm, CI/CD) in a SaaS/multi-tenant environment — this is assumed, not a differentiator
  • Working understanding of core cryptographic primitives (symmetric/asymmetric encryption, hashing, digital signatures, TLS/PKI fundamentals)
  • Demonstrated security-first engineering habits: secure coding practices, threat modeling, code review discipline

Qualifications

  • Experience with leading fix implementation and release coordination across engineering, product, and test/release teams.
  • Proficiency in deep-dive product security investigations and root-cause analysis spanning design, code, configuration, and operational layers.
  • Exploit analysis and proof-of-concept development that distinguishes real exploitability from theoretical risk.
  • Familiarity with SDLC integration, CI/CD pipelines, SaaS threat models, and secure development practices.
  • Experience leading a CVE disclosure process, including CVE assignment, scoring (CVSS), and advisory publication.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a PSIRT or similar function for a major software or SaaS platform.
  • Recognized expertise in product security incident response, vulnerability research, or application security within a software or SaaS environment.
  • Experience conducting vulnerability assessments on the ServiceNow platform.
  • Experience with emerging threats: AI-specific attack vectors, software supply chain security, and SDLC tooling security.

title: Staff FinOps Analyst
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Team 

Join FinOps Governance team that is part of the Global Cloud Services organization. 

You’ll apply your expertise in AI cost management and data-driven optimization to lead programs that bring accountability and control to ServiceNow’s AI investments. Working closely with engineering teams building AI-powered skills and experiences, cloud finance leadership, and provider relationships with Azure, AWS, GCP, Anthropic and OpenAI, you’ll be the connective tissue between technical usage and financial discipline. 

About the role 

We are looking for a Staff FinOps Analyst to drive financial accountability and optimization across ServiceNow’s AI spend. This senior individual contributor role combines deep AI infrastructure literacy, data-driven governance, and cross-functional program leadership to ensure our AI investments are managed with the same rigor as our cloud infrastructure. The ideal candidate understands the economics of LLMs as well as they understand engineering and will thrive operating independently while engaging VP-level stakeholders with confidence and clarity. 

What you get to do in this role:

  • Define, track, and systematically review AI cost and usage KPIs; identify anomalies and outliers that signal potential waste, misuse, or optimization opportunities. 
  • Design and operate an anomaly detection framework to surface suspiciously high AI usage across models and skill teams, and engage engineering collaboratively to investigate and remediate. 
  • Quantify, prioritize, and propose cost optimization opportunities—evaluating levers such as PTU vs. pay-as-you-go trade-offs, model tiering, context reduction, and caching—and drive them to measurable outcomes. 
  • Design preventive governance controls so that cost anomalies and overruns, once identified, are systematically prevented from recurring. 
  • Define and implement AI spend guardrails in coordination with cloud and LLM providers: set up budgets, configure alerts, manage commitment structures, and ensure contractual rate accuracy. 
  • Coordinate the AI FinOps governance program across engineering, finance, and cloud provider relationships—maintaining a clear operating model with documented standards and a regular review cadence. 
  • Prepare and deliver VP-level reporting and presentations on AI cost trends, optimization progress, and forward-looking forecasts, translating technical data into clear financial narratives. 
  • Operate as a self-starter and self-sufficient program owner: define scope, manage stakeholders, and drive workstreams to completion with minimal direction. 

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • 8 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 6 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years experience; or equivalent experience.
  • Strong working knowledge of LLM pricing models, multi-cloud AI services (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP Vertex AI), and AI cost optimization levers. 
  • Proficiency in data analysis using SQL and/or Python to build KPI frameworks, identify usage anomalies, and communicate findings through data visualization. 
  • Hands-on experience with multi-cloud cost governance across AWS, Azure, and GCP, including budget management, alerting, tagging, and billing API familiarity. 
  • Proven cross-functional collaboration skills with engineering teams—ability to communicate cost impact, influence technical decisions, and drive efficiency improvements. 
  • Outstanding communication and executive presentation skills; comfortable preparing and delivering briefings to VP-level audiences on complex technical and financial topics. 
  • Self-directed and highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams independently in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (Computer Science, Engineering, Finance, Mathematics, or related). 

Nice to have: 

  • Experience with AI optimization techniques: model routing strategies, prompt engineering, context length management, batch inference, and caching.

title: Sr. Staff Product Manager, AI-Native IT Service Management
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the team 

Service Operations is where enterprises find out whether their technology actually works. An outage starts, someone gets paged, a bridge call spins up, and the first twenty minutes go to working out what broke rather than fixing it. 

Our team owns the products that close that gap: incident and major incident, problem and root cause, change, on-call, and Notify. The people using them go well beyond the service desk, from application, platform, infrastructure, and network teams to DevOps and SRE groups who get alerted around the clock and the major incident commanders pulling everyone onto one call. Thousands of the largest IT organizations run their operations on these products. We are rebuilding them AI-native, not AI-assisted, with agents that triage, correlate, and resolve, and with people moving from doing the work to directing it. Our goal is Zero Service Outage. 

About the role 

You will own a piece of that portfolio outright: what good looks like for it, who it is for, and whether we are honestly there yet. Zero Service Outage is the goal, and the work is making it true for the customers who run their operations on these products every day. 

The interesting part of this job is not the model. It is the environment it runs in. Service operations data is the messiest data in the enterprise: half-populated CMDBs, incident descriptions written in a hurry at 2am, alert noise from a dozen monitoring tools, and naming conventions that differ by region. An agent that triages perfectly against a clean eval set can behave very differently against a real customer’s incident stream, for reasons that have nothing to do with reasoning ability. Understanding why, and designing for it, is the job. 

We also carry an installed base. Customers run today’s experience in production, and moving them onto an AI-native one is not a UI refresh. It is a change to how their IT team works, who approves what, and what an operator trusts an agent to do unsupervised. You will be making calls about what we carry forward, what we leave behind, and what we have to earn the right to automate. 

How we work is changing as fast as what we build. Prototype instead of describing the idea. Put a working demo in front of people instead of a slide about a demo. Draft the spec, stand up a rough eval harness, pull your own data. ServiceNow invests in state-of-the-art tooling and expects you to use it. Product managers are better positioned than anyone to lead that shift, and part of this role is pulling the team around you into it. 

What you get to do in this role 

  • Own an AI-native ITSM product end to end, from the customer problem through launch criteria to how it performs in production. 

  • Set product strategy for the Service Operations portfolio that supports ServiceNow’s growth toward $10B+ in revenue. 

  • Build, not just specify. Prototype the interaction, stand up the eval harness, and get into the agent execution logs to understand what happened on the runs that failed. 

  • Define what good means for an autonomous agent in an operational context where the cost of a wrong action is a second outage. Hold the line on it with engineering and have the honest conversation about what we can defensibly promise. 

  • Work with design partners across the teams that run on this: service desk, application and infrastructure support, DevOps and SRE, and major incident command. Build in their environment against their real incidents, changes, and RCAs, then turn what you learn into something that generalizes to the next thousand customers. 

  • Own your outcome metrics, such as time to resolve, change failure rate, and repeat incidents, in partnership with Customer Success, and make sure the instrumentation exists to show whether what you shipped moved them. 

  • Align with peer product managers so the team is working on the right things at the right time and guide multiple teams through ambiguous product development without losing sight of the unified vision. 

  • Write the strategy, the specs, and the analysis yourself. 

  • Coach other product managers. This is a senior role on a small team, and how you raise the people around you counts as much as what you ship. 

Qualifications

Qualifications 

  • 12+ years of software product management experience, including a track record of shipping complex enterprise products that customers love and that drive meaningful business outcomes. 

  • Have owned an AI-native product end to end and been the person accountable for its quality bar. The ownership is what matters, not the years. 

  • Know what enterprise-grade means for AI: the quality bar, the guardrails, the telemetry, and the work of earning a customer’s trust before they hand an agent real authority. 

  • Have working knowledge of IT service operations: how incidents, changes, and on-call actually run, and why operations teams are slow to trust automation. You know these domains well enough to identify what should change fundamentally, not just incrementally. 

  • Comfortable with platform concepts such as workflow orchestration, workspace design, Flow Designer, and extensibility patterns. You can engage in architecture discussions and make informed trade-offs. 

  • Experience working with large enterprises that have complex customizations, compliance requirements, and high expectations. 

  • Experience defining and capturing product requirements, from customer insights and market analysis to detailed user stories and product roadmaps that align stakeholders and guide execution. 

  • Deep curiosity about customer needs and a track record of building authentic customer relationships. 

  • Ability to drive solution development through systems thinking and to serve as a product lead and mentor for more junior team members. 

  • Experience integrating AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving, whether through AI-powered tools, workflow automation, or analysis of AI-driven insights. 

Preferred qualifications 

  • Depth in IT service operations: incident and major incident, change, problem and RCA, CMDB, on-call, or AIOps. You have been on the bridge call, or close enough to know how the first thirty minutes go. 

  • Agent evaluation: eval set design, LLM-as-judge, and closing the gap between offline results and production behavior. 

  • Hands-on prototyping and analysis. You work in the tooling, the data, and the logs rather than describing them. 

  • Zero-to-one experience, where the users, the quality bar, and the economics all had to be worked out at once. 

  • Experience migrating a large installed base onto a materially different experience. 

  • AI-native working habits that are already default, and evidence that you have changed how a team around you works. 

  • Familiarity with other enterprise workflow platforms such as Salesforce, Jira Service Management, Freshworks, and BMC.

title: Staff Reliability Engineer - Veza
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Veza is the pioneer in identity security, purpose-built to answer the fundamental question enterprises face: who can and should take what action on what data. Veza's Access Graph platform maps an organization's entire identity ecosystem  across users, groups, roles, policies, permissions, and resources  providing deep visibility and control over human, non-human, and agentic identities across SaaS, cloud, on-prem, and custom applications. With over 30 billion access permissions under management, global enterprises including Blackstone, Expedia, and Wynn Resorts trust Veza to manage privileged access monitoring, non-human identity security, access entitlement management, and next-generation identity governance. 

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Veza is now part of the ServiceNow family, with the acquisition closing in March 2026. The combination brings together Veza's AI-native Access Graph with ServiceNow's AI Control Tower and agentic workflows, enabling organizations to enforce end-to-end identity security rooted in the principle of least privilege across applications, data, cloud environments, and AI agents.  For engineers joining Veza today, this means the scale and resources of an enterprise platform company, with the product velocity and mission-driven focus of a security innovator at a pivotal moment in the industry.

descriptionHtml:

Job Description

ServiceNow's Advanced Technology Group is a customer-focused innovation team building intelligent software and AI-powered work experiences. We combine AI workers, workflows, chat, knowledge, and integrations to make complex enterprise operations accessible to everyday users.

Our researchers, applied scientists, engineers, designers, and product managers have a dual mission: build end-to-end products for customers while experimenting with and de-risking the technologies that will shape how people work.

The role

We are looking for an experienced, backend-leaning full-stack engineer who can take a problem and solve it across the product and system. You will build customer-facing capabilities spanning the browser, APIs, data models, realtime infrastructure, asynchronous jobs, and external integrations.

You will have the autonomy to shape problems, make sound architectural decisions, and own work from idea through production. We value engineers who are self-directed, pragmatic, curious, and uncompromising about security and software quality.

What you will do

  • Build AI-powered product capabilities across React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and shared contracts.
  • Own features from product definition and system design through implementation, testing, deployment, and operation.
  • Design secure APIs, authorization rules, data models, and backward-compatible migrations.
  • Build reliable asynchronous and realtime workflows using queues, pub/sub, jobs, schedules, and WebSockets.
  • Develop enterprise integrations involving OAuth, webhooks, rate limits, external APIs, and vendor failures.
  • Protect tenant boundaries and validate untrusted input across HTTP, sockets, queues, and AI tool execution.
  • Build, deploy, and operate services running on AWS and Kubernetes.
  • Diagnose production behavior using logs, traces, metrics, databases, and message brokers.
  • Work closely with product, frontend, AI, and platform engineers while independently driving execution.
  • Help evolve our engineering practices as AI changes how software is designed and built.

Qualifications

What we are looking for

  • Strong TypeScript fundamentals and production experience with React and Node.js.
  • A track record of driving complex, customer-facing features end to end with visible product impact.
  • Strong SQL and relational data-modeling skills, including transactions, indexes, and migrations.
  • Experience with asynchronous or distributed systems: queues, pub/sub, WebSockets, retries, and idempotency.
  • Sound API, schema, and backward-compatibility judgment.
  • Strong security instincts for multi-tenant authorization, credentials, uploads, and external input.
  • Experience with automated unit, integration, API, and end-to-end testing.
  • Product judgment and comfort operating without heavy specification or process overhead.
  • High ownership: you stay accountable for reliability and customer outcomes after the code ships.

AI Development Lifecycle

Hands-on ADLC experience is mandatory. You must have shipped software using AI across discovery, design, implementation, testing, review, documentation, and production debugging—not only used a coding assistant occasionally.

You know how to validate AI-generated work, define evaluations and regression criteria, manage context, and account for nondeterminism, hallucinations, latency, cost, privacy, and security. You retain human ownership of the architecture, code, and customer outcome.

You can design reliable AI execution paths involving prompts, structured outputs, agents, tools, approvals, schemas, authorization, retries, observability, and failure recovery. Model output is treated as untrusted input, and consequential actions require explicit authorization.

Our technology

TypeScript, React, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Sequelize, Redis, RabbitMQ, Socket.IO, Zod, Nx, Vite, Vitest, Playwright, Sentry, AWS, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Cursor, and Linear.

Experience with every technology is not required. Python, FastAPI, AI agent runtimes, MCP, enterprise integrations, and direct AWS infrastructure experience are valuable but not mandatory.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Job Description

Global Partnerships & Channels (GPC) 

At ServiceNow, we put AI to work for people. Our AI platform connects any AI, any data, and any workflow to help organizations work smarter, move faster, and reinvent how business gets done. Global Partnerships & Channels extends that impact through a worldwide ecosystem of strategic, technology, cloud, service, and solution partners. 

Role Overview 

The Executive Administrative Assistant (EAA) to the GPC Leader is a highly trusted administrative partner responsible for maximizing the effectiveness, productivity, and operating capacity of a global executive leading one of ServiceNow’s most strategic and fast-moving organizations. 

This is an AI-forward executive support role requiring demonstrated proficiency with AI-enabled Executive Assistant (AI EA) tools and platforms, in addition to broader AI and automation capabilities. The successful candidate already uses AI EA tools as an integrated part of how they manage executive calendars, scheduling, meeting preparation, follow-up, travel, communications, task management, and executive-office workflows. 

We are looking for someone who can show how they have personally used AI EA technology to improve the way an executive office operates—not simply someone who is familiar with AI, uses a general-purpose AI assistant, or is interested in learning these tools. 

The GPC Leader operates at an exceptionally fast pace across a global ecosystem of ServiceNow executives, customers, partners, industry leaders, and employees. Priorities can shift rapidly and often require immediate action. The EAA must operate with exceptional agility, adaptability, flexibility, judgment, and precision while maintaining accuracy and continuity across a constantly changing executive agenda. 

This role goes well beyond traditional calendar administration. The EAA is a force multiplier for the executive, combining exceptional executive support capabilities with AI EA technology, automation, and modern productivity practices to anticipate needs, eliminate friction, create operating leverage, and continually improve how work gets done. 

What You’ll Do 

AI EA Tools, Automation & Executive Productivity 

  • Demonstrate advanced, hands-on proficiency using AI-enabled Executive Assistant tools and platforms specifically designed to support executive administration and executive-office workflows. 

  • Integrate AI EA tools into daily work to improve complex scheduling, calendar optimization, meeting preparation, briefing and context development, action and commitment tracking, follow-up, travel coordination, communications, and executive workflow management. 

  • Use AI EA capabilities to anticipate conflicts, identify scheduling and workflow dependencies, surface outstanding actions, organize executive priorities, and reduce administrative friction. 

  • Determine which work is best performed through specialized AI EA tools, broader AI platforms, workflow automation, or direct human judgment and intervention. 

  • Build and continually improve an AI-enabled administrative operating model that increases executive capacity while maintaining exceptional accuracy, discretion, responsiveness, and stakeholder experience. 

  • Identify repetitive or inefficient administrative processes and redesign them using AI EA capabilities, automation, integrations, templates, and other productivity technologies. 

  • Apply appropriate quality controls to AI-supported work, independently validating outputs and maintaining accountability for accuracy, confidentiality, and final execution. 

  • Remain current on emerging AI EA technologies and proactively evaluate and adopt capabilities that can measurably improve executive and administrative productivity. 

Executive Calendar, Time & Priority Management 

  • Own a highly complex, dynamic global executive calendar involving C-suite leaders, senior internal executives, customers, strategic partners, industry leaders, and employees. 

  • Manage the calendar as a strategic business tool, ensuring executive time is aligned to the highest-value business, customer, partner, talent, and leadership priorities. 

  • Make rapid, thoughtful decisions when priorities change, understanding what can move, what cannot, who needs to be informed, and what downstream implications must be addressed. 

  • Anticipate conflicts, preparation requirements, decision points, travel implications, and follow-up needs before they become issues. 

  • Reprioritize quickly and confidently in an environment where the executive’s schedule may change multiple times in a day. 

  • Protect focus time while preserving the flexibility required of a highly visible global leader. 

Internal & External Executive Engagements 

  • Orchestrate internal and external executive engagements from initial request through preparation, execution, and follow-up. 

  • Coordinate engagements with ServiceNow executives, customers, partners, industry leaders, external organizations, and other high-priority stakeholders. 

  • Ensure the executive enters critical engagements with the right context, objectives, participants, materials, logistics, and preparation. 

  • Maintain visibility to commitments and follow-up resulting from executive engagements and ensure actions move forward quickly. 

  • Coordinate across executive offices and external organizations to create a highly professional, responsive, and seamless stakeholder experience. 

  • Represent the GPC Leader with discretion, confidence, sound judgment, and strong executive presence. 

GPC Leadership & Operating Rhythm 

  • Enable the operating rhythm of the GPC leadership team, including leadership meetings, business reviews, planning sessions, executive offsites, talent discussions, company events, and key partner engagements. 

  • Partner closely with the Chief of Staff to translate business priorities into an effective executive cadence and use of the leader’s time. 

  • Maintain a working understanding of GPC priorities, key decisions, leadership commitments, and upcoming milestones so administrative decisions can be made with appropriate business context. 

  • Connect meetings, decisions, commitments, and follow-up rather than treating individual calendar events as isolated activities. 

  • Anticipate what the leader and leadership team will need next and initiate action without waiting for direction. 

Cross-Functional Executive Office Partnership 

  • Work closely with the Chief of Staff, HR Business Partner, Executive Communications, Finance, Strategy, and other key functions to coordinate and sequence executive priorities. 

  • Serve as a highly effective connector across teams, ensuring information, decisions, requests, and follow-up move at the pace required by the business. 

  • Coordinate executive communications, leadership forums, company events, talent engagements, organizational activities, and external commitments. 

  • Establish strong working relationships with executive assistants across ServiceNow and with the offices of customers, partners, and other external executives. 

Global Travel & Executive Logistics 

  • Manage complex domestic and international travel, including rapidly changing itineraries, executive meetings, partner/customer engagements, events, and associated logistics. 

  • Anticipate travel dependencies and resolve issues quickly, often with limited notice and across multiple time zones. 

  • Integrate travel, meetings, preparation, and executive priorities into a cohesive plan rather than managing each independently. 

  • Remain highly responsive when critical executive needs or schedule changes require flexibility outside traditional working hours. 

Qualifications

What You Bring 

  • Certification in Certified Administrative Professional (CAP) or equivalent administrative credential preferred. 

  • 7+ years of progressive experience supporting senior executives, preferably at the SVP, EVP, or C-suite level in a global technology, high-growth, or similarly fast-paced environment. 

  • Demonstrated proficiency with AI-enabled Executive Assistant (AI EA) tools and platforms. This is a core requirement of the role—not simply general familiarity or fluency with AI. 

  • Proven experience personally incorporating AI EA tools into executive administrative workflows such as complex calendar and scheduling management, meeting preparation, executive briefing, action tracking, follow-up, travel, communications, and productivity management. 

  • Ability to provide specific examples of AI EA tools used, the executive-administration problems addressed, how the tools were incorporated into daily workflows, and the resulting improvements in speed, efficiency, accuracy, or executive capacity. 

  • Broader proficiency with generative AI, workflow automation, and productivity technologies, with the ability to combine these capabilities with specialized AI EA tools. 

  • Demonstrated success supporting a global executive operating at exceptional speed, with complex stakeholder demands and priorities that can change rapidly. 

  • Exceptional agility, adaptability, and flexibility, including the ability to reprioritize and execute quickly without sacrificing accuracy. 

  • Exceptional attention to detail and a demonstrated record of accuracy in high-volume, high-velocity executive environments. 

  • Advanced ability to manage highly complex global calendars and make independent prioritization decisions with limited direction. 

  • A productivity and continuous-improvement mindset: instinctively identifies opportunities to simplify, automate, standardize, eliminate unnecessary work, and improve how the executive office operates. 

  • Exceptional judgment, discretion, executive presence, and ability to manage highly sensitive and confidential information. 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and confidence engaging with senior internal executives, customers, partners, and external stakeholders. 

  • A highly anticipatory working style—the ability to recognize what is needed, understand implications, and act before being asked. 

  • Ability to remain composed and highly effective amid ambiguity, urgency, last-minute change, and competing demands. 

What Success Looks Like 

  • The GPC Leader has more capacity because of this partnership. Executive time is focused on the highest-value priorities, administrative friction is reduced, and the executive office operates at extraordinary speed without sacrificing accuracy or stakeholder experience. 

  • AI EA technology is embedded in the day-to-day operation of the executive office. Specialized AI EA tools, broader AI capabilities, and automation are intentionally applied to reduce administrative burden, accelerate execution, improve accuracy, strengthen follow-through, and increase executive capacity. 

  • Internal and external executive engagements are exceptionally well orchestrated. The leader has the right context at the right time; stakeholders receive timely, professional engagement; commitments do not get lost; and changes are absorbed without unnecessary disruption. 

  • The EAA is a trusted extension of the GPC Leader—able to keep pace, anticipate what is coming, adapt immediately when circumstances change, and continually increase the productivity of the executive and broader leadership team. 

Why This Role Matters 

Global Partnerships & Channels is central to how ServiceNow expands customer value, scales innovation, and brings the power of the ServiceNow AI platform to market through a global partner ecosystem. The Executive Administrative Assistant is a critical enabler of that mission—creating focus, connectivity, productivity, and operating leverage for the GPC Leader and leadership team.

That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

At ServiceNow, we put AI to work for people. IT operations is where that matters most. When services slow down or fail, everyone feels it. Our IT Operations Management (ITOM) and AIOps portfolio helps organisations see their whole IT estate, predict issues before they reach users, and resolve them automatically. It sits at the heart of our Autonomous IT story.

Our UK & Ireland Specialist Presales Solution Consulting organisation is going through a significant evolution. We’re bringing separate specialist teams together into one organisation with one way of working: one front door for requests, deployment based on deal criteria rather than availability, and a shared set of measures across every domain. We’re doing it because customers buy the platform, not individual products, and our specialists need to show up as one team.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager to lead our ITOM and AIOps presales specialists through this change. This is a quota-carrying sales leadership role and a first-line people leadership role in equal measure. You’ll build a high-performing team, bring them with you through a new operating model, and make sure their expertise reaches the deals and customers where it makes the biggest difference.

How you’ll work with sales

Your team brings specialist depth when an opportunity needs it, and you share accountability for the result. In practice, that means:

  • Partnering with the Solution Consulting Directors in each core industry area: Enterprise Industries, Financial Services, Public Sector, Energy Telco & Media, and Ireland. Together you’ll agree which accounts and opportunities to prioritise, how specialists get engaged and how you’ll measure impact.
  • Running a criteria-based engagement model. Requests come through a single front door, self-service assets are offered first where they fit, and specialist time goes to the opportunities with the highest stage, value and complexity.
  • Building capability across the Core SC community so they can lead standard ITOM conversations and demos with confidence, spot when a specialist is needed, and bring your team in early.
  • Creating pipeline with the regions through specialist-led activities such as hands-on workshops, customer connect sessions and value labs, rather than waiting for opportunities to arrive.

You’ll succeed through influence, not reporting lines. Comfort with matrix management is essential.

What you get to do in this role

Lead and grow a high-performing team

  • Recruit, coach and develop a team of ITOM and AIOps specialists, growing experienced and emerging talent alike.
  • Set clear expectations, run consistent operational and team cadences, and hold the team to a high standard for customer impact and follow-through.
  • Build belonging and momentum in a team that’s adapting to a new way of working.
  • Develop specialists into T-shaped consultants: deep in ITOM and AIOps, and fluent in how IT operations connects to asset management, security, risk and data across the platform.

Champion the change

  • Actively support and help the Specialist Solution Consulting operating model. Translate it for your team, raise concerns early and model the behaviours you expect.
  • Establish consistent rules of engagement with Core SC, Account Executives and partners.
  • Be data driven using data to support business execution and change

Win deals and drive consumption

  • Lead from the front on strategic opportunities, owning the technical win for ITOM and AIOps alongside Core SC and sales.
  • Shape cross-domain, platform-level solutions with specialist peers in asset management, Risk & Security, Employee Workflows and Data & AI.
  • Make the CMDB a strength in every customer conversation. It’s the foundation of the ServiceNow platform, and your team brings the deepest expertise in the discovery and service mapping that keep it accurate.
  • Partner with our Customer Excellence Group to help customers adopt and get value from capabilities they already own.

Enable and influence

  • Own the ITOM and AIOps contribution to UK & Ireland SC enablement, from Level 100 for every Core SC to Level 200 champion tracks. Ensure your team is operating at Expert Level 300.
  • Track record of building and maintaining reusable assets: demos, use cases, discovery guides and points of view.
  • Develop industry points of view on IT operations, and represent ServiceNow at customer, partner and industry events.
  • Work closely with EMEA ITOM peers, product management, partners and enterprise architects.

How you’ll be measured

This is a sales role. You’ll carry a quota for ITOM and AIOps across the UK & Ireland, alongside the shared specialist measures that every domain uses.

Quota attainment

Revenue delivered for ITOM and AIOps across the UK & Ireland

Tech-win conversion

How often specialist engagement turns into a technical win

Specialist-sourced pipeline

New pipeline your team creates with the regions

Consumption uplift

Customers getting more value from what they already own

Team capacity

How well specialist time goes to the deals that matter most

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

Experience and leadership (essential)

  • 10+ years in IT operations, pre-sales, solution engineering or technical consulting, ideally in enterprise software.
  • 5+ years leading pre-sales or technical teams as a people manager.
  • A consistent track record of attaining and exceeding quota in a technical sales leadership role, including managing complex sales cycles from start to finish.
  • Proven track record of change management execution.
  • Experience in a matrix organisation, influencing senior peers and sales leaders without direct authority.
  • Strong coaching and talent development skills, including hiring and succession planning.
  • Confidence presenting to and advising senior IT leaders such as C-suite, Heads of IT Operations and Heads of Infrastructure.

IT operations expertise (essential)

A deep, practical understanding of modern IT operations, including:

  • Observability and monitoring, including event, metric and log correlation.
  • AIOps: noise reduction, anomaly detection and predictive operations.
  • Discovery, service mapping and configuration management (CMDB).
  • Incident, problem and change practices, with ITIL 4 or equivalent.
  • Site reliability engineering and service reliability concepts.
  • Hybrid and multi-cloud operations, and IT automation.
  • The ability to connect operational capability to business outcomes: availability, cost, risk and user experience.

ServiceNow experience (desirable, not essential)

  • Hands-on or pre-sales experience with ServiceNow ITOM, such as Discovery, Service Mapping, Event Management, AIOps, Service Reliability Management, CMDB and CSDM, and Digital End-User Experience.
  • ServiceNow certifications such as Certified System Administrator, or Certified Implementation Specialist in Discovery, Service Mapping or Event Management.

If you’ve done this on another observability, monitoring or IT operations platform, we want to hear from you.

Ways of working

  • A data-driven approach to running a team and a pipeline.
  • Curiosity about AI and agentic operations, and the ability to explain them simply.
  • Willingness to travel up to 40% across the UK and Ireland.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Overview

The AI Application Software Engineer designs, builds, ships, and operates applications whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret user intent, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the user's behalf. In Field Service Management, this means building AI-native experiences for scheduling, dispatch, and service workflows that automate routine work, escalate exceptions, and improve customer outcomes.

This is a hands-on, forward deployed role for a senior engineer whose first instinct is AI — someone who can shape ambiguous customer problems into precise specifications, author the instructions and prompts that govern agent behavior, build the application and integrations around them, and prove through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly. This is not a machine learning or AI research role; you will not train foundation models. You own what ships, whether a human or an agent produced it.

What You Get to Do

•      Build AI-native applications. Design and ship applications built around agentic behavior across Field Service Management — scheduling, dispatch, and workflows that reason over context, automate routine work, and escalate exceptions.

•      Work AI-first in delivery. Direct coding agents to build, refactor, and test; use AI to think more sharply in front of customers; and apply it as part of everyday engineering practice rather than as a side tool.

•      Deliver forward deployed. Work embedded in customer environments, tuning instructions and evaluation sets on the ground, using AI to compress turnaround without cutting quality.

•      Author and maintain agentic instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern agent behavior — treating them as reviewed, regression-covered engineering artifacts.

•      Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic behavior. Design and operate golden datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring, CI gates, drift detection, adversarial testing, and grounding checks that make change safe.

•      Design conversational experiences. Build experiences that hold context, confirm before consequential actions, and hand off cleanly to humans.

•      Collaborate across product, UX, and documentation. Bring the AI-first instinct into cross-functional partnerships, not just your own code.

•      Own quality and safety in production. Monitor containment, hallucination, prompt injection, and data leakage, then feed failures back into specifications and evaluation sets.

Qualifications

Experience
A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production software, including hands-on delivery of AI-native application features that real users depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts, designing AI-driven workflows, and building evaluation and testing for non-deterministic behavior is required. Experience with chat experiences is required; voice or multi-channel experience is strongly preferred. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity is required; prior forward deployed experience is an advantage.

Education
Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 3 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work experience.

Key competencies
•      Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing. Good to have technologies like  HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Java. 

•      AI-native application development. Hands-on experience with agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling latency, cost, and failure.
•      Agentic instruction and prompt engineering. Demonstrated skill with instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, structured outputs, grounding, citation, graceful failure, and disciplined iteration against measured outcomes.
•      Specification precision. Ability to define a problem rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements it correctly, and to judge when to solve it in code, in instructions, or by delegating.
•      Customer-facing delivery with AI-native speed. Comfort working directly with customers under real constraints, using AI to cut turnaround, and communicating capability and risk credibly to non-engineers.
•      AI safety and data handling. Working knowledge of prompt injection, data leakage, over-broad tool access, and unsafe autonomous action, translated into concrete guardrails and least-privilege controls.

Desired experience
•      Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.
•      A platform-level view. Experience with agent runtimes, context engineering, retrieval, and memory.
•      Domain depth. Experience in Field Service Management, scheduling, or workforce management is valued but not required; the right engineer can learn the domain.
•      Evaluation and observability tooling. Experience with evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production transcripts at scale.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the team 

The CRM & Industry Workflows (CRM&I) engineering organisation builds the products that make ServiceNow's CRM vision real: Workplace Service Delivery, Customer Service Management, Field Service Management, Sales & Order Management, and the shared CRM Foundation that underpins them all. Our teams operate from IDC, AMS, and EMEA, and our work spans the full spectrum — from foundational platform capabilities to the agentic experiences that define how enterprises serve their employees and customers. 

We are in the middle of a fundamental shift. AI is not a layer we are adding on top — it is the new baseline. We are rewriting how products are built, how engineers work, and what 'done' means. If you are energised by that shift and want to lead teams that are living it, read on. 

The role 

This Director of Software Engineering leads the Workplace engineering pillar within CRM&I. You will own Workplace Service Delivery and its adjacent integrations with CSM and FSM — building the employee and customer facing experiences that handle millions of service interactions across our largest enterprise customers. 

What makes this role distinct from a traditional engineering director role is the AI-native mandate. You will not manage teams that use AI as a productivity tool — you will build and lead an organisation that operates as an AI-native engineering system. Your engineers work more like architects and verifiers than individual contributors typing every line: they decompose problems into agent-sized tasks, curate the context that makes agent output reliable, and own the verification harnesses that ensure correctness at scale. 

You will report to the Senior Director, CRM&I Engineering and work closely with Workplace product management, platform engineering, and senior stakeholders to shape and deliver the Workplace roadmap for the next three to five years. 

What you get to do 

Lead and develop an AI-native engineering organisation 

  • Build and lead two to three engineering managers who coach their teams to operate with AI-native practices as the default — not the exception. 

  • Model and scale the shift from implementation-speed metrics to judgment metrics: specification quality, architectural soundness, and verification rigour. 

  • Cultivate a culture where engineers own the correctness of output whether a human or an agent produced it, and are accountable for autonomous decision quality in production. 

Drive the Workplace product roadmap 

  • Partner with product management and UX to define, own, and execute the Workplace Service Delivery roadmap — including employee self-service, request management, and WSD×CSM/FSM integration. 

  • Translate ambitious product goals and ambiguous problem statements into precise, testable specifications that both engineers and AI agents can act on with high accuracy. 

  • Make sound architectural and sequencing decisions early, before agent workstreams begin, and course-correct quickly when output diverges from intent. 

Build reliable AI-native systems 

  • Design the verification and guardrail harnesses — automated tests, evaluation suites, CI/CD quality gates, and least-privilege execution environments — that make agent-generated output trustworthy at scale. 

  • Oversee context engineering across your teams: instruction files, architectural decision records, golden examples, and agent-readable documentation that drive reliable results from AI coding agents. 

  • Own AI reliability in production: monitor for hallucinations, behavioural drift, and safety regressions; maintain agent observability; and implement rollback mechanisms when autonomous behaviour deviates from intent. 

Raise the bar on quality, security, and delivery 

  • Set and hold the standard for enterprise-grade software quality — accessible, progressive, and responsive web and mobile experiences at the scale our customers demand. 

  • Champion security-minded engineering practices specific to AI-integrated systems: prompt injection defence, secret and data leakage controls, and tool-access governance. 

  • Treat the development process itself as a product: trace failures back to missing specs or context gaps, refine evaluation harnesses, and raise team-wide throughput and reliability. 

Develop the next generation of engineering leaders 

  • Mentor and grow engineering managers and senior engineers, investing in their technical depth, leadership range, and AI-native fluency. 

  • Create a talent environment where engineers who are energised by the AI-native shift can build careers through some of the most advanced systems in enterprise software.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role 

Experience 

  • 15+ years of experience designing and shipping scalable enterprise software products, with significant time in technical leadership roles. 

  • Demonstrated track record of building and leading engineering teams that have delivered real production systems using AI-native methods — agentic coding tools, AI-assisted workflows, and autonomous agent architectures. 

  • Experience in CRM, ITSM, workplace service delivery, or related enterprise domains preferred. 

AI-native engineering fluency 

  • Agentic AI and autonomous systems. Hands-on experience designing and operating autonomous agent systems — planning loops, dynamic tool invocation, memory management, execution policies, and multi-agent collaboration — that select and sequence actions reliably in production. 

  • Context engineering. Skill in designing what information models receive, when it is retrieved, and how context evolves. Includes assembling instruction files, documentation, examples, and architectural constraints, as well as architecting retrieval systems, vector databases, and long-term memory frameworks. 

  • Verification and harness design. Experience building the guardrail systems that make agent output reliable at scale: property-based and mutation tests, evaluation suites, CI/CD quality gates, and provenance and permission controls. 

  • Outcome evaluation. Ability to develop measurable frameworks — benchmarks, golden datasets, continuous evaluation pipelines, and drift detection — that hold production AI to the same rigour as deterministically testable software. 

  • Security and reliability mindset. Working knowledge of risks specific to AI-integrated systems: prompt injection, sensitive-data leakage, tool-access governance, and model abuse, translated into concrete engineering controls. 

Leadership and collaboration 

  • Strong written and verbal communication — able to operate as a credible technical voice with product, platform, and executive stakeholders. 

  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities and make clear decisions under uncertainty without waiting for perfect information. 

  • Conviction to influence product vision and roadmap, paired with the humility to listen, learn, and adapt. 

Forward deployed engineering 

  • Customer-embedded delivery. Experience leading or participating in forward deployed engineering (FDE) engagements — working on-site or in close collaboration with strategic customers to accelerate time-to-value, co-develop solutions, and unblock adoption of product capabilities. 

  • Translating customer context into product decisions. Ability to synthesise what you learn at the customer boundary — pain points, integration constraints, workflow gaps, and adoption blockers — into precise product requirements and engineering priorities that feed back into the core roadmap. 

  • Executive and technical credibility with customers. Comfortable presenting architecture decisions, roadmap trade-offs, and delivery progress to both customer engineering leads and C-suite stakeholders, earning trust through technical depth and clear communication rather than sales framing.

  • Cross-functional coordination in a customer environment. Experience coordinating across product, sales, and professional services teams while embedded with a customer — navigating competing priorities, escalation paths, and success handoffs without losing engineering focus. 

Technical depth 

  • Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, and modern software development practices. Good to have technologies like  HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Java. 

  • Solid data modelling background — relational and otherwise — with experience building systems where data model quality is a first-class concern. 

  • Proficiency with AI/ML fundamentals: model training and evaluation, embeddings, and the probabilistic failure modes of LLMs, sufficient to reason about and debug model-driven behaviour in production. 

Even better if you have 

  • Experience with the ServiceNow platform — scoped application architecture, Glide APIs, or platform engineering at scale. 

  • Hands-on exposure to multi-tenant SaaS architecture and the operational realities of shipping to thousands of enterprise customers simultaneously. 

  • Experience building and operating agentic systems in a regulated or enterprise-compliance context. 

  • Prior experience managing distributed engineering organisations across time zones. 

  • Direct experience leading forward deployed engineering engagements — co-developing solutions alongside strategic customers, accelerating adoption of complex capabilities, and feeding field learnings back into the product roadmap.

We provide competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a professional environment built on collaboration and inclusion. This is an organisation where people with strong aptitude and conviction grow fast — working on some of the most advanced enterprise technology in the world, with teams that take the craft seriously. 

If you want to lead engineering at the frontier of what AI-native product development actually looks like in production — not in a lab, but at enterprise scale — this is the role.

This remote position will be reporting to Director, Internal Audit Management. You’ll also help build the next version of Internal Audit by designing AI-enabled tools and automations that change how audits get done, not just using the tools others hand you. 

We have a tight team environment where support, loyalty, and honest feedback are the currency. ServiceNow employees are expected to be self-starting, proactive, and thrive in a fast-paced environment. 

What you get to do in this role: 

  • Support planning and scoping of operational and integrated audits across business and IT operations. Complete assignments efficiently and timely. 
  • Conduct walkthroughs, evaluate process design, and perform controls testing across both business processes and IT systems, consistently delivering quality audit work papers that support and substantiate audit observations. 
  • Identify manual or repetitive steps in the audit lifecycle and build AI-enabled solutions to automate them, such as prompt workflows, AI agents, scripts, or data pipelines for evidence gathering, testing, and workpaper drafting. 
  • Use data analytics and AI to test full populations when possible, identify control gaps, quantify risk exposure, and deliver data-driven insights to management. 
  • Document and share what you build so the team can reuse it, and help shape Internal Audit’s AI playbook. 
  • Assist in producing high-quality Internal Audit reports by clearly drafting audit issues and developing valid conclusions resulting in process and internal control improvements, while considering implementation requirements, cost, and stakeholder feedback. 
  • Timely and effective communication with audit leads on audit status, escalations, issues, and reporting. 
  • Perform action tracking follow-up with management for Audit Committee reporting purposes. 
  • Participate in major business initiatives and proactively advise and assist the business on key risks, control environment, and change initiatives. 
  • Contribute to the evolution of Internal Audit methodology, automation, and reporting, including ServiceNow IRM to scale audit coverage and quality. 
  • Responsible for internal stakeholder engagement, including the development of working relationships with key stakeholders and proudly representing the Internal Audit function. 

Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you have:

  • A passion for Internal Audit and strong desire to be part of a stellar IA team! 
  • Minimum 4-year degree (or US equivalent) from an accredited university; degree in Management Information Systems, Finance and Accounting strongly preferred. 
  • Minimum of 5 years’ work experience, with 3 years at a public accounting firm (Big 4 or national consulting firm preferred), including experience in internal auditing, external auditing, SOX, operations and process improvement. 
  • Demonstrated experience auditing both IT general controls and application controls, and business operational processes. Comfort moving fluidly between technology and business-process audits, including within the same integrated engagement. 
  • Understanding of data governance and privacy compliance, and the ability to apply system architecture knowledge to the processes being reviewed. 
  • Understanding of risks and controls in modern technology environments. Awareness of AI/GenAI governance and model risk considerations. 
  • Builder track record: you’ve built something, such as a tool, automation, script, or AI workflow, that solved a real problem in your work. Be ready to walk us through it. 
  • Hands-on experience with generative AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) beyond basic chat, such as building custom prompts, agents, or automated workflows. 
  • Good understanding of business and operations, strong analytical and project management skills. 
  • Proficiency in Excel and process mapping tools. Hands-on experience with data analytics tools such as Power BI. Experience with SAP preferred.                   
  • Strong critical thinking and analytical skills; ability to identify and conduct root cause analysis.                                                           
  • Excellent verbal, written, oral communication and presentation skills. 
  • Ability to work both independently and as a team member. 
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks concurrently, efficiently and effectively with minimal oversight. 
  • Familiarity with the ServiceNow platform, including IRM modules, a strong plus 
  • (Preferred) At least one of the following certifications: CISA, CISM, CIA, CPA 
  • Prefer candidates with exposure to a high growth and/or rapidly changing technology enterprise.
